# RAVET feature catalogue

Current capabilities and their limits. Implemented features remain within
the stated scope; public APIs are provisional. Prototype integrations need
further validation. Planned and deferred capabilities are not usable features.

See [Getting started](getting-started.md) for commands,
[work status](WORK_STATUS.md) for executed validation, and
[maintenance](maintenance.md) for status definitions and update rules.

## Feature overview

| Feature | Status | Behavior or intent |
|---|---|---|
| [Portable processor lifecycle](#portable-processing) | Implemented | Validated preparation, variable and zero-frame blocks, reset, deactivation, and atomic rejection with silence on faults. |
| [Allocation-free no_std processing foundation](#embedded-foundation) | Implemented | Existing portable audio/event/lifecycle/schema contracts work without std or an allocator, with pure-Rust parameter math and target-gated snapshots. |
| [Fixed-capacity embedded audio adaptation](#embedded-fixed-block-adapter) | Implemented | An explicit no_std adapter owns fixed planar f32 scratch, preflights complete interleaved f32/i16/i32 blocks and preserves event timing, fault silence and backing tails. |
| [Embedded gain and native Arduino processing subset](#embedded-reference-bridges) | Prototype | An allocation-free Rust stereo gain and caller-owned C ABI accompany a header-only C++11 stereo adapter/reference for Arduino cores without a Rust archive. |
| [Extended processing capabilities](#extended-processing) | Implemented | Portable f32/f64 processor specializations support bounded multichannel/auxiliary buses, borrowed event output and latency/tail declarations; CLAP forwards validated block-start transport. |
| [Borrowed planar audio buffers](#audio-buffers) | Implemented | Safe in-place and separate input/output f32/f64 views validate channel lengths and expose active frames while preserving backing tails; stereo frame mapping selects storage outside the sample loop. |
| [Sample-timed input events](#input-events) | Implemented | Bounded parameter values/gesture boundaries/modulation amounts, note and validated MIDI short-message events use stable IDs, physical values, ordered offsets, and preserved same-frame order. Zero-frame events use offset zero. |
| [Portable transport context](#transport-context) | Implemented | Process blocks carry optional positions, tempo, playback state, and a discontinuity indication. |
| [Extended block-start transport metadata](#extended-block-start-transport) | Prototype | Optional portable details and checked bidirectional CLAP conversion preserve recording, active loop, pre-roll, signature, bar and tempo increment metadata. |
| [No-input instrument contract](#instrument-contract) | Implemented | Foundation represents mono/stereo instruments without audio inputs; a test instrument exercises note timing and output initialization. |
| [Bounded coherent word snapshots](#coherent-snapshots) | Implemented | Fixed atomic word arrays provide one-attempt coherent reads, complete publications, and conditional updates that preserve newer control restores. |
| [Prepared acyclic processor routing](#prepared-audio-graphs) | Prototype | Owned portable f32/f64 nodes run in compiled topological order with channel mixing, parallel dry/wet routes, prepared latency compensation, bounded scratch and conservative tail declarations. |
| [Prepared dynamic graph handoff](#prepared-graph-handoff) | Implemented | One prepared FIFO f32/f64 graph replaces the active graph per valid block, with bounded ownership queues and control-thread retirement. |
| [Explicit graph event routing](#explicit-graph-events) | Implemented | Filtered host/node generated events share audio/event topology, bounded stable sample-offset merging and complete host output publication. |
| [Explicit prepared graph audio-owner sessions](#explicit-graph-audio-owner-sessions) | Implemented | Optional no-op processor session hooks bracket static/dynamic graph processing with non-Send owner guards, reverse stop/rollback and stopped control retirement. |
| [Typed graph stages and shared-control mono histories](#typed-chain-shared-mono-composition) | Implemented | Concrete const-index tuple stages reuse canonical graph execution, guarded audio ownership and explicit bypass; generic mono kernels share one prepared control object with separate native histories. |
| [Prepared CLAP f32 main audio graph node](#hosted-clap-f32-main-graph-node) | Implemented | Main-activated native audio maps through bounded prepared f32 graph scratch, owner-confined sessions and stopped-token main deactivation/recovery. |
| [Prepared CLAP native f64 main audio graph node](#hosted-clap-f64-main-graph-node) | Implemented | A separate f64 factory validates advertised port support before activation and keeps native/graph samples wide through shared owner-confined lifecycle and stopped main retirement. |
| [Prepared CLAP packed native audio ports in graphs](#hosted-clap-packed-audio-graph-ports) | Implemented | Explicit f32/f64 factories preserve separate native port/channel boundaries while graph routes address directional summed channel indices, including sidechain inputs and auxiliary outputs. |
| [Opt-in hosted CLAP block-start transport](#hosted-clap-block-start-transport) | Implemented | Checked portable context maps into flagged native tempo/beat/seconds fields for explicitly enabled stopped f32/f64 graph nodes, preserving independent steady clocks and rejection before native rendering. |
| [Prepared CLAP graph global parameter input](#hosted-clap-graph-parameter-input) | Implemented | Explicit f32/f64 factories validate product-to-native parameter identities/ranges on main, then deliver exact ordered global values through bounded audio-owner process or zero-frame flush. |
| [Prepared CLAP graph global parameter output and builder](#hosted-clap-graph-parameter-output) | Implemented | A preparation builder selects independent fixed port/transport/parameter profiles; bounded mapped native global output, including read-only values, publishes through portable graph event routes. |
| [Prepared CLAP graph selected note and MIDI input](#hosted-clap-graph-note-input) | Implemented | The f32/f64 preparation builder validates an explicit native note-port index/dialect and delivers ordered mixed parameters, CLAP notes, short MIDI/MPE or framed UMP through fixed audio-owner input slots. |
| [Prepared CLAP graph selected performance output](#hosted-clap-graph-note-output) | Implemented | An independent selected native output index/dialect publishes representable CLAP notes, short MIDI/MPE or framed UMP through shared bounded graph event slots and explicit routes. |
| [Guarded main-owned editors for native graph nodes](#hosted-clap-graph-editor-ownership) | Implemented | Retained native graph control creates an exclusively borrowed PluginEditor while separately owned audio may run; bounded main callback servicing preserves restart/process requests. |

| [Bounded generated output from graph workers](#buffered-graph-worker-event-output) | Implemented | Fresh buffered graph renders publish caller-owned generated-event prefixes once, independent of partial audio queue publication, with exact prepared output capacity. |
| [Complete bounded event batches for graph worker/control handoff](#graph-worker-complete-event-queues) | Implemented | Fixed SPSC batches atomically publish validated events with opaque tags/context; prepared consumer storage retains immutable batches until explicit acknowledgement for input or output delivery. |
| [Bounded CLAP audio-owner processing handoff](#bounded-native-audio-owner-handoff) | Implemented | Main-activated stopped processors enter a non-Send native audio owner, replace through bounded SPSC retirement and return stopped tokens for main-thread deactivation. |
| [Prepared interleaved audio handoff ring](#audio-handoff-ring) | Implemented | Unique SPSC endpoints atomically transfer whole interleaved f32 frame prefixes with explicit backpressure and untouched consumer tails; unique-producer Drop permanently publishes retirement for stopped-finalization proof. |
| [Native-precision CLAP main-bus effects and instruments](#clap-native-main-bus) | Prototype | Prepared main-bus adapters map 0..64 inputs/1..64 outputs at native f32/f64 precision, global parameters, selected-port short MIDI and validated block-start transport. |

## Implemented capabilities

<a id="portable-processing"></a>

### Portable processor lifecycle

Validated preparation, variable and zero-frame blocks, reset, deactivation, and atomic rejection with silence on faults.

**Limits:** One main bus and up to eight auxiliary buses, up to 64 channels per direction, f32/f64 processor specialization; each implementation declares its subset. Public APIs are provisional. Real-time obligations are implementor responsibilities.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet/src/lib.rs), [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs), [`examples/gain/tests/processing.rs`](../examples/gain/tests/processing.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/architecture.md`](../docs/architecture.md), [`docs/decisions/0001-portable-processing.md`](../docs/decisions/0001-portable-processing.md).

<a id="embedded-foundation"></a>

### Allocation-free no_std processing foundation

Existing portable audio/event/lifecycle/schema contracts work without std or an allocator, with pure-Rust parameter math and target-gated snapshots.

**Limits:** Default std feature retains desktop mappings; Cargo feature unification applies. Pinned libm 0.2.16; snapshots require native 64-bit atomics. Existing signal/graph/device/editor/runtime crates remain outside this allocator-free subset. Cross checks are library evidence, not board/deadline support.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/Cargo.toml`](../crates/ravet-foundation/Cargo.toml), [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/lib.rs), [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/parameter.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/parameter.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs), [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/parameters.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/parameters.rs), [`scripts/check-embedded.py`](../scripts/check-embedded.py).

**Documentation:** [`docs/embedded-projects.md`](../docs/embedded-projects.md), [`docs/decisions/0152-embedded-processing.md`](../docs/decisions/0152-embedded-processing.md).

<a id="embedded-fixed-block-adapter"></a>

### Fixed-capacity embedded audio adaptation

An explicit no_std adapter owns fixed planar f32 scratch, preflights complete interleaved f32/i16/i32 blocks and preserves event timing, fault silence and backing tails.

**Limits:** Const channels/frames, exact configured layout, no auxiliary buses/generated events. f32 internal precision; packed 24-bit conversion is consumer-owned. Processor allocation/ownership obligations and hardware drivers/DMA/cache/scheduling remain explicit; no board or deadline guarantee.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-embedded/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-embedded/src/lib.rs), [`crates/ravet-embedded/Cargo.toml`](../crates/ravet-embedded/Cargo.toml).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-embedded/tests/blocks.rs`](../crates/ravet-embedded/tests/blocks.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/embedded-projects.md`](../docs/embedded-projects.md), [`docs/architecture.md`](../docs/architecture.md).

<a id="extended-processing"></a>

### Extended processing capabilities

Portable f32/f64 processor specializations support bounded multichannel/auxiliary buses, borrowed event output and latency/tail declarations; CLAP forwards validated block-start transport.

**Limits:** 64 channels per direction, eight auxiliary buses, caller-owned fixed output capacity. Processors declare their subset; gain supports f32/f64 without auxiliary/generated events, while generic CLAP bridges map native main/aux buses and bounded events. Other-format generic bus/output/latency mappings and mid-block transport remain separate.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/audio.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/audio.rs), [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs), [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/event.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/event.rs), [`crates/ravet-clap/src/transport.rs`](../crates/ravet-clap/src/transport.rs), [`examples/gain-clap/src/lib.rs`](../examples/gain-clap/src/lib.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/extended_processing.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/extended_processing.rs), [`examples/gain-clap/tests/bridge.rs`](../examples/gain-clap/tests/bridge.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/extended-processing.md`](../docs/extended-processing.md), [`docs/decisions/0017-extended-processing.md`](../docs/decisions/0017-extended-processing.md).

<a id="audio-buffers"></a>

### Borrowed planar audio buffers

Safe in-place and separate input/output f32/f64 views validate channel lengths and expose active frames while preserving backing tails; stereo frame mapping selects storage outside the sample loop.

**Limits:** Borrowed planar views support f32/f64 and multichannel storage. No interleaved view or implicit conversion. Stereo mapper still requires two outputs and at most two inputs.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/audio.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/audio.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs), [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/stereo_mapping.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/stereo_mapping.rs), [`examples/gain/tests/processing.rs`](../examples/gain/tests/processing.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/decisions/0001-portable-processing.md`](../docs/decisions/0001-portable-processing.md), [`docs/decisions/0011-stereo-frame-mapping.md`](../docs/decisions/0011-stereo-frame-mapping.md).

<a id="input-events"></a>

### Sample-timed input events

Bounded parameter values/gesture boundaries/modulation amounts, note and validated MIDI short-message events use stable IDs, physical values, ordered offsets, and preserved same-frame order. Zero-frame events use offset zero.

**Limits:** Bounded output events, UMP codecs/transport and MIDI voice policy are separate capabilities. Gain ignores performance events and unknown parameter IDs; each format bridge declares its mappings.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/event.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/event.rs), [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs), [`examples/gain/tests/processing.rs`](../examples/gain/tests/processing.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/decisions/0001-portable-processing.md`](../docs/decisions/0001-portable-processing.md).

<a id="transport-context"></a>

### Portable transport context

Process blocks carry optional positions, tempo, playback state, and a discontinuity indication.

**Limits:** Gain is transport-independent. CLAP forwards validated block-start playing/position/tempo fields and detects seeks across accepted callbacks. Additional details carry validated block-start recording/active-loop/pre-roll, signature, bar and BPM-per-sample increment; no extrapolation or mid-block updates.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/event.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/event.rs), [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/architecture.md`](../docs/architecture.md), [`docs/decisions/0002-clap-backend.md`](../docs/decisions/0002-clap-backend.md).

<a id="instrument-contract"></a>

### No-input instrument contract

Foundation represents mono/stereo instruments without audio inputs; a test instrument exercises note timing and output initialization.

**Limits:** Contract fixture only; a separate portable sine processor now consumes the contract. No CLAP instrument export.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/processor.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/contracts.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/architecture.md`](../docs/architecture.md).

<a id="coherent-snapshots"></a>

### Bounded coherent word snapshots

Fixed atomic word arrays provide one-attempt coherent reads, complete publications, and conditional updates that preserve newer control restores.

**Limits:** Targets with 64-bit atomics only; allocation-free operations do not establish deadlines. Callers encode and validate words and retain the previous snapshot on contention. Coalesces publications, with no event queue or retry policy. Generation must not wrap across an operation.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/src/snapshot.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/src/snapshot.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-foundation/tests/snapshot.rs`](../crates/ravet-foundation/tests/snapshot.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/snapshots.md`](../docs/snapshots.md), [`docs/decisions/0008-word-snapshots.md`](../docs/decisions/0008-word-snapshots.md).

<a id="prepared-graph-handoff"></a>

### Prepared dynamic graph handoff

One prepared FIFO f32/f64 graph replaces the active graph per valid block, with bounded ownership queues and control-thread retirement.

**Limits:** 1..4 slots per pending/retired queue; exact initial config and path latency required. Retirement backpressure keeps current rendering. No old-history migration, tail drain, crossfade, feedback routing or aggregate graph/node memory guarantee. Endpoint teardown and retired destruction belong outside callbacks; no native deadline claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-graph/src/dynamic.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/src/dynamic.rs), [`crates/ravet-graph/Cargo.toml`](../crates/ravet-graph/Cargo.toml).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-graph/tests/dynamic.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/tests/dynamic.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/audio-graphs.md`](../docs/audio-graphs.md), [`docs/decisions/0056-prepared-graph-handoff.md`](../docs/decisions/0056-prepared-graph-handoff.md).

<a id="explicit-graph-events"></a>

### Explicit graph event routing

Filtered host/node generated events share audio/event topology, bounded stable sample-offset merging and complete host output publication.

**Limits:** 4096 event edges, 1024 input/output events per node/host, shared 64 MiB audio/event scratch cap. Duplicate edges duplicate events. Offsets are not audio-latency delayed. Overflow disables graph and clears host outputs; earlier nodes may have advanced. No feedback, automatic state/timing alignment or native deadline claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-graph/src/events.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/src/events.rs), [`crates/ravet-graph/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/src/lib.rs).

<a id="explicit-graph-audio-owner-sessions"></a>

### Explicit prepared graph audio-owner sessions

Optional no-op processor session hooks bracket static/dynamic graph processing with non-Send owner guards, reverse stop/rollback and stopped control retirement.

**Limits:** Explicit opt-in only; existing adapters/unguarded portable behavior unchanged. Start failure must leave its node stopped, prior starts roll back; dynamic rejected candidates retire while old rendering continues. End/retain guards before control transfer/deactivation; no native port/event mapping/device scheduling/migration/crossfade/tail draining/platform/deadline guarantee.

<a id="typed-chain-shared-mono-composition"></a>

### Typed graph stages and shared-control mono histories

Concrete const-index tuple stages reuse canonical graph execution, guarded audio ownership and explicit bypass; generic mono kernels share one prepared control object with separate native histories.

**Limits:** Native f32/f64, effect-only1..64 equal main channels, tuple1..8, <=65536 frames at construction (prepare may still refuse by the Graph scratch cap), chain<=1024 broadcast input events/no generated or auxiliary events; mono rejects all events/auxiliary buses. Checked4MiB record/kernel-Vec payload excludes caller-owned and Graph memory. Bypass freezes/skips events but retains declared latency/tail without audible delay compensation. Stopped mutation requires reprepare; child faults retain original GraphStatus with BackendFailure facade/no rollback. Manual Processor start must be paired with stop_audio on its starting thread before transfer, deactivation, extraction or drop (caller obligation, no automatic cleanup): prepare and the stopped getter refuse while a manual owner is live, deactivate/into_stages/Drop panic; the non-Send session is preferred. Shared control object immutability while prepared, kernel nonfinite policy and callback/panic obligations remain with the implementor; Graph denies unsafe except its audited private typed storage module; other workspace crates retain their existing policy. Isolated qualification passes74 runtime tests+21 doctests/strict lint/docs/fmt; Miri unavailable, no physical/deadline claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-graph/src/typed.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/src/typed.rs), [`crates/ravet-graph/src/mono.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/src/mono.rs).

Main-activated native audio maps through bounded prepared f32 graph scratch, owner-confined sessions and stopped-token main deactivation/recovery.

**Limits:** Zero/one main port per direction matching 1..64 channels, frames1..65536, node-owned scratch<=32MiB outside graph cap; no events/auxiliary/editor/active parameter mapping; f64 uses its separate factory. Explicit declared timing, one-shot node after deactivation, consumer core request scheduling and orderly control lifetime. Backend faults may advance histories; no implicit sleep/tail drain/restart/other-format/device scheduling/general third-party/platform/deadline guarantee.

Retained native graph control creates an exclusively borrowed PluginEditor while separately owned audio may run; bounded main callback servicing preserves restart/process requests.

<a id="buffered-graph-worker-event-input"></a>

### Bounded event input for buffered graph workers

Fresh graph-worker renders accept ordered staged input and acknowledge consumption; retained queue suffix pumps leave new events/context untouched without repeating native input.

**Limits:** No-input f32 fixed blocks, 0..1024 input slots, empty-output convenience methods; separate pump_io carries configured output. Explicit compatible node profiles. <a id="buffered-graph-worker-event-output"></a>

### Bounded generated output from graph workers

Fresh buffered graph renders publish caller-owned generated-event prefixes once, independent of partial audio queue publication, with exact prepared output capacity.

**Limits:** No-input f32 fixed blocks, 0..1024 output slots and explicit graph/node routes/profiles. Pending publication leaves storage untouched and returns zero output count; caller uses only valid returned prefix. Wrong fresh capacity rejects before nodes. Graph faults suppress faulty queue publication/prefix but cannot roll back native histories. No telemetry queue/replay/control delivery, block/device-clock correlation, GUI/recovery scheduler or deadline promise. Loaded public fixture synthetic macOS arm64 evidence only.

<a id="graph-worker-complete-event-queues"></a>

### Complete bounded event batches for graph worker/control handoff

Fixed SPSC batches atomically publish validated events with opaque tags/context; prepared consumer storage retains immutable batches until explicit acknowledgement for input or output delivery.

**Limits:** 1..65536 fixed frames, 0..4096 events, 1..64 queued batches plus one retained consumer batch; queue values<=32MiB plus retained events, outside graph/native caps; graph render batches remain limited to 1024 events per direction. Invalid/full publishes no prefix, observed disconnect rejects. No tag uniqueness, timestamp/clock conversion, retiming/replay, wait/wake, GUI/recovery or native transport policy. Producer teardown preserves batches for drain; stop/join owners before endpoint drop. Loaded synthetic fixture macOS arm64 evidence only, no device/host/deadline claim.

<a id="bounded-native-audio-owner-handoff"></a>

### Bounded CLAP audio-owner processing handoff

Main-activated stopped processors enter a non-Send native audio owner, replace through bounded SPSC retirement and return stopped tokens for main-thread deactivation.

**Limits:** CLAP/Clack host handlers, queues1..4, consumer tags/config/ports/event/latency compatibility and request/fault/sleep policy. Native start failures retain old processing; no tail drain/crossfade/migration/graph-device routing/other-format/crash isolation/general third-party compatibility/deadline guarantee. Keep matching main instances alive; finish and token/endpoint destruction outside callbacks.

<a id="audio-handoff-ring"></a>

### Prepared interleaved audio handoff ring

Unique SPSC endpoints atomically transfer whole interleaved f32 frame prefixes with explicit backpressure and untouched consumer tails; unique-producer Drop permanently publishes retirement for stopped-finalization proof.

**Limits:** 1..64 channels, power-of-two 1..65536 frame capacity; prepare/drop allocate, push/pop do not. Caller chooses drop/retry/silence and worker/device lifecycle; live/leaked producers cannot prove retirement. No automatic seek, transport, recording scheduler or deadline guarantee.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-audio-file/src/ring.rs`](../crates/ravet-audio-file/src/ring.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-audio-file/tests/streams.rs`](../crates/ravet-audio-file/tests/streams.rs), [`crates/ravet-audio-file/tests/recording.rs`](../crates/ravet-audio-file/tests/recording.rs), [`crates/ravet-device/tests/recording_worker.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/tests/recording_worker.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/audio-files.md`](../docs/audio-files.md), [`docs/decisions/0026-audio-streams.md`](../docs/decisions/0026-audio-streams.md).

<a id="prepared-interpolated-peak-estimates"></a>

### Prepared interpolated peak estimates

Explicit finite Kaiser-sinc 4/8/16-phase peak measurement with immutable CONTROL design, single/1..64-channel streaming owners, complete stopped tail and separate sample/source/work observations.

**Limits:** Integer rates 8000..768000 Hz (validated metadata only: coefficients depend on factor, half-width and beta, 216 rate/profile admissions are 36 coefficient profiles, and the library cannot verify the actual source clock), half-width 32..512, beta 0..16, callbacks 1..65536, defensive 8 MiB aggregate prepared budget that admitted profiles (about 665,000 bytes at the maximum) cannot reach. Native f32 source widens into f64 measurement; finite grid/window estimate without standards or continuous-maximum certification. Live readings can be below the sample peak until finish. Whole-call preflight reserves full tail counter headroom. Nonfinite measured silence with per-channel flag, source audio untouched, genuine amplitude overflow visible and distinct, no hidden subnormal flush. Explicit 2L tail after stopped ownership; no Drop I/O, hardware/deadline or loudness/LRA claim. Near-Nyquist fixture (36 profile combinations; its half-sample centre lies on every grid) has exactly 12 tolerance failures, all half-width 32: about +0.2952 dB over-reading at beta 0 and -0.769 to -1.189525 dB under-reading at beta 6/12/16; the +0.2/-0.4 dB interval is not widened. Selected external FFmpeg grid differs at high source rates; its upstream source attribution is not newly verified.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-signal/src/true_peak.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/true_peak.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak.rs), [`crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak_graph.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak_graph.rs), [`crates/ravet-signal/tests/true-peak-decimal.csv`](../crates/ravet-signal/tests/true-peak-decimal.csv), [`crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak_decimal_oracle.py`](../crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak_decimal_oracle.py), [`crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak_ffmpeg_oracle.py`](../crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak_ffmpeg_oracle.py), [`crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak_example_admission.py`](../crates/ravet-signal/tests/true_peak_example_admission.py), [`crates/ravet-signal/examples/true-peak-file.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/examples/true-peak-file.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/signal-processing.md`](../docs/signal-processing.md), [`docs/decisions/0263-prepared-interpolated-peak-estimates.md`](../docs/decisions/0263-prepared-interpolated-peak-estimates.md).

<a id="prepared-calibrated-loudness-range"></a>

### Prepared calibrated loudness and loudness range

Explicit calibrated K-weighted M/S/I/LRA with rational 10-Hz windows, independent channel roles, full log-domain programme records, retrospective gates/ranks, programme pause/resume and exclusive stopped analysis.

**Limits:** Every integer rate 8000..768000 Hz, roles 1..64, callbacks 1..65536 and independent I/LRA record capacities 1..1000000 (at most 24000000 array bytes plus owner today); a defensive 32 MiB aggregate guard is checked before reservation and on actual capacity, and is not reachable by current caps before allocation. Native f32 widens into f64 measurement; rate-dependent response retained, stated only as selected-transfer facts at named frequencies (not a wideband, profile-accuracy or conformity bound); the 48 kHz stages have an independent numeric anchor, other rates share the oracle's calibration facts. Odd-rate floor grid, artificial tail and nearest zero-based percentile policy are own choices, without standards certification. Whole-call preflight and full optional-tail headroom; finite filter overflow invalidates readings and reports with original committed coordinate while raw record slices stay readable as diagnostic history only, nonfinite source measured silence, audio untouched, Excluded channels run no filter and keep no K history. CONTROL-only scan/sort/analysis, explicit ceil(3Fs/2) LRA tail (first policy wins; no tail when nothing admitted) with exact capacity refusal, no implicit Drop work, concurrent UI, advanced spatial metadata, physical/timestamp/acoustic or deadline claim. Selected FFmpeg rank/histogram differences and the 0.233355 LU LRA mismatch retained.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-signal/src/loudness.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/loudness.rs), [`crates/ravet-signal/src/filter.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/filter.rs).

<a id="scoped-native-floating-control"></a>

### Explicit scoped native floating-control ownership

A separate optional numerical boundary provides thread-bound no_std scopes with exact prior control/status restoration, actual flush-profile admission and failure-owned optional Processor integration.

**Limits:** Ordinary OS AArch64 FPCR/FPSR and x86_64 SSE2 MXCSR only; actual DAZ/FTZ/AH/trap admission. Preserve isolates scope-created status as well as retaining controls. Compiler/library expression semantics, x87/half/SVE, physical x86 support, automatic SIMD, host/device and deadline claims are excluded from this receipt. Manual AUDIO hook pairing remains the consumer obligation; child faults do not imply history rollback.

<a id="explicit-packed-vector-slice-family"></a>

### Explicit packed float values and prepared vector slices

Explicit Scalar/NEON/SSE2 f32x4/f64x2 values and lane masks provide full arithmetic, comparison, bit selection, transforms and declared reductions; prepared no_std slice operations admit complete prefixes and channel banks before edits.

**Limits:** Widths4/2 and maxima1..1048576, channel-bank gain1..64, immutable selected backend; native admission is compile-time aarch64+neon or x86_64+sse2 only; actual native CPU/math policy applies without an automatic denormal guard. Scalar sqrt uses direct exact libm0.2.16. Clip endpoint ordering observes active input flushing. Slice arithmetic is bit-qualified only under the no-flush Preserve profile. Right-preference ties/NaNs and unfused/width-dependent reduction order are explicit. Native execution qualified on AArch64, x86_64 separately through Rosetta; no physical x86, AVX/half/SVE/integer-vector, SIMD ABI/register residency, whole FFT/FIR vectorization, universal speedup/deadline or host/device claim.

<a id="native-canonical-table-identity"></a>

### Canonical native table acquisition

Runtime acquisition preserves exact immutable processor/parameter/cache/audio-state/state/telemetry table addresses across exports and transitive companions.

**Limits:** Same concrete family/precision and loaded originating library only; CONTROL acquisition/lifetime and exact type/pointer obligations remain. NativeProcessor::entry is no longer const-callable. Metadata validation can allocate under its existing contract; no table interning registry or relaxed structural equivalence. Offline cross-codegen/default-consumer tests do not establish host or deadline support.

<a id="clap-host-request-handoff"></a>

### Coalesced CLAP host requests

Core restart/process/callback requests use an atomic coalesced mailbox with explicit deferral and bounded main-thread callback service.

**Limits:** Consumers own restart/process transitions, wakeups and native scheduling. Mailbox must match instance. No automatic audio/device lifecycle or extension-specific host request handling; repeated kinds coalesce.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-host/src/requests.rs`](../crates/ravet-host/src/requests.rs), [`crates/ravet-host/examples/inspect.rs`](../crates/ravet-host/examples/inspect.rs).

<a id="hosted-clap-parameters"></a>

### Bounded hosted CLAP parameters

Owned stable-ID/plain-value metadata, atomic refresh, validated reads and explicit inactive parameter edits borrow the live instance.

**Limits:** Control-thread 1..4096 maximum, no cookie caching/normalization. Consumers own rescan, output queues and acknowledgement checks. No active automation scheduler, automatic refresh or persistence fallback; separate opt-in ParameterHost handles extension requests.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-host/src/parameters.rs`](../crates/ravet-host/src/parameters.rs), [`crates/ravet-host/examples/inspect.rs`](../crates/ravet-host/examples/inspect.rs).

<a id="clap-host-parameter-requests"></a>

### Deferred CLAP host parameter callbacks

Opt-in parameter host handlers defer coalesced rescan/flush and bounded exact-ID clear actions while preserving core lifecycle requests.

**Limits:** 64 distinct main-thread clear IDs between drains; overflow retains prefix and requires consumer reconciliation/rejection. Main mailbox owner-thread only. No automatic reference storage, refresh/recovery, active automation or native lifecycle scheduler.

<a id="hosted-clap-audio-configuration"></a>

### Bounded hosted CLAP audio metadata

Owned inactive directional port snapshots validate IDs/layout/precision/pairs, with optional main-thread latency and audio-owner tail queries.

**Limits:** 0..9 ports per direction/1..64 channels, 256-byte names/types. Inactive inspection and atomic refresh; missing audio extension means no ports, missing timing stays None. No configuration negotiation, automatic compensation or native graph integration; separate ProcessingHost receives change notifications.

<a id="clap-host-audio-change-requests"></a>

### Deferred CLAP audio configuration callbacks

Opt-in combined processing host advertises port/latency/tail and parameter callbacks, with atomic coalesced audio-change handoff and explicit deferral.

**Limits:** Consumer owns deactivation, correct-thread timing query, metadata refresh and prepared route rebuilding. No ordered history, automatic restarts/wakes, compensation or native graph scheduling.

<a id="clap-parameter-registration"></a>

### Borrowed CLAP parameter registration

Portable schemas supply validated complete CLAP count/info metadata with exact physical bounds/defaults, ordered module/process policy and a sole binary bypass; gain consumes the registration.

**Limits:** 0..1024 parameters; names 255/module paths 1023 UTF-8 bytes without NUL, valid CLAP IDs; discrete ranges require contiguous unit integers. Explicit global/scoped flags remain consumer policy; no cookies, value storage, formatting/flush/rescan or automatic plug-in generation/lifecycle.

<a id="zero-volume-note-expression"></a>

### Explicit zero-volume note expression

Portable and native f64 linear volume accepts zero mute and preserves signed zero and positive subnormals through complete event conversion and worker handoff.

**Limits:** Finite0..4; no change to native v1 tags/layout. CLAP remains strictly positive0<x<=4: selected zero input rejects, zero generated output rejects whole delivery before any host write, with rendered DSP/audio retained. No epsilon substitution, voice application/allocator or VST3/DAW support follows from this scalar contract. Provisional APIs; older consumers may reject zero.

<a id="sample-wise-waveshapers"></a>

### Custom transfer functions and clipping waveshapers

Inline caller-owned f32/f64 transfer functions run once per sample, with explicit f64 hard-clip, tanh and cubic soft-clip constructors and in-place/separate block processing.

**Limits:** No implicit drive/gain, smoothing, DC removal, oversampling or alias-free/deadline claim. Wrapper has no history/latency/tail or heap actions; custom function resources/state/real-time behavior belong to callers. Exact block lengths preflight before output/calls; empty no-op. Built-ins propagate NaN and bound infinities; custom nonfinite policy is unchanged. Cubic endpoints are +/-2/3, not unity-normalized.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-signal/src/waveshaper.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/waveshaper.rs), [`crates/ravet-signal/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/lib.rs).

<a id="prepared-biquad-filters"></a>

### Prepared biquad filters

Validated normalized stable coefficients and six Q-based and two slope-based shelving cookbook designs drive f64 transposed direct-form II processing and control-thread response inspection.

**Limits:** One channel per instance; no higher-order designer, coefficient smoothing, audio sanitization, denormal policy or deadline guarantee. Finite rate/frequency/Q/gain bounds and unrepresentable stability margins reject. Shelves use gain -120..120 dB and slope (0,1], distinct from Q; numerical extreme accuracy/headroom remains caller responsibility.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-signal/src/filter.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/filter.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-signal/src/filter.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/filter.rs), [`crates/ravet-signal/tests/prepared.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/tests/prepared.rs), [`crates/ravet-signal/tests/shelves.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/tests/shelves.rs).

<a id="fixed-filter-cascades"></a>

### Fixed cascades and even-order Butterworth designs

Fixed 1..16 validated second-order sections provide f64 cascading, history-preserving replacement and even-order low/high pass Butterworth preparation.

**Limits:** One channel, orders 2..32, finite rate/strict interior cutoff; unrepresentable stages reject. No odd orders, band designs, automatic order/family selection or smoothing. Arbitrary stage gains/headroom/product overflow and nonfinite/denormal policies belong to callers; offline numerical/heap evidence, no deadline claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-signal/src/cascade.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/cascade.rs), [`crates/ravet-signal/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/lib.rs), [`crates/ravet-signal/src/filter.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/filter.rs).

<a id="linear-state-variable-filter"></a>

### Prepared simultaneous-output state-variable filter

One-channel f64 trapezoidal integrators return low/band/high outputs together with prepared coefficients and retained histories.

**Limits:** Rate positive/finite, cutoff/rate 1e-6..=0.499999, Q 0.1..=100; raw band gain Q. No smoothing/nonlinear saturation/denormal policy/arbitrary-modulation stability/deadline guarantee. Nonfinite audio propagates and extreme finite amplitudes can overflow.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-signal/src/state_variable.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/state_variable.rs), [`crates/ravet-signal/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/lib.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/signal-processing.md`](../docs/signal-processing.md), [`docs/decisions/0095-linear-state-variable-filter.md`](../docs/decisions/0095-linear-state-variable-filter.md).

<a id="linkwitz-riley-crossover"></a>

### Prepared fourth-order Linkwitz–Riley crossover

Fixed-storage one-channel f64 low/high branches use two identical Butterworth sections each, with half-amplitude cutoff and all-pass recombination.

**Limits:** Finite positive rate, cutoff strictly between DC/Nyquist; unrepresentable stable designs reject. Equal-length caller buffers preflight atomically; empty no-op, reset clears histories and unsmoothed replacement retains them. Unity summed magnitude is not input waveform identity. LR4 electrical profile only, no loudspeaker alignment, other orders, automatic routing/modulation, nonfinite/denormal/headroom or native deadline claim.

Precomputed radix-two f64 FFT transforms exact-length caller-owned complex buffers forward or normalized inverse without callback allocation.

Rectangular/Hann/Hamming/Blackman/Blackman-Harris, symmetric/periodic; no sampled peak/automatic gain correction, optimized real-only/SIMD/overlap-add/native deadline claim.

Uniform f64 overlap-add response partitions and a prepared input spectrum ring produce streaming long-response convolution independent of caller block sizes.

<a id="native-convolution-schedules"></a>

### Native-precision zero-latency, uniform and nonuniform convolution banks

Prepared f32 and f64 convolution engines run zero-latency direct-head, uniformly delayed and two-stage nonuniform partitioned schedules with 1..64-channel diagonal banks and a native f32 FFT; info reports exact latency, tail, stage layout and storage.

**Limits:** 1..262144 finite taps per channel; head/partition power of two 16..4096, late partition power of two head..16384; maximum block 1..65536; aggregate numeric budget 1 byte..256 MiB per engine or bank checked before fallible allocation and against actual capacities (allocator overhead excluded), so max-length f64 two-stage banks hold at most 14 channels. Fixed two-stage schedule, not optimal partitioning. Diagonal channels only: no true-stereo matrix, crossfeed or linked normalization. Engines perform no loading, rate conversion, trim, normalization or live replacement themselves (see impulse-response-preparation and live-convolution-transitions). Nonfinite and denormal values propagate. Direct head O(head) per sample, bursty FFT boundaries; selected-profile rounding observations only, no deadline, SIMD, DAW, device or platform claim.

<a id="impulse-response-preparation"></a>

### Explicit source-rate impulse-response preparation

Memory or WAV/AIFF/compressed-file responses are prepared at their source rate for a target engine rate with explicit sinc conversion (gain and delay policies), channel mapping, linked threshold trimming with recorded offsets and peak/energy normalization with reported gain, then built into native f32/f64 convolution engines or banks.

**Limits:** Memory path always built in ravet-signal; the file path requires ravet-audio-file's default-disabled resampled-playback feature. Planar f64 1..64 channels, 1..4194304 source frames, rates 1..768000 Hz; existing 1025-phase Blackman integer-rate sinc only (even taps 16..256, ratio 1/16..16), whole-frame delay removal with reported fractional remainder; prepared length 1..262144; result/staging/table budget 1 byte..256 MiB checked before allocation (file path adds source storage). Select/identity mapping only, no mixing or true-stereo matrix; linked trim/normalization only; energy sums are power-of-two scaled (overflowing gain refused NonFinite, underflowing UnrepresentableGain). Existing sinc table allocation is infallible (budgeted). Whole-call refusal, no partial result; file reads have no rollback. CONTROL/worker allocation. Analytic references at selected rate pairs only; no spectral guarantee, deadline, DAW or platform claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-signal/src/impulse_response.rs`](../crates/ravet-signal/src/impulse_response.rs), [`crates/ravet-audio-file/src/impulse_file.rs`](../crates/ravet-audio-file/src/impulse_file.rs).

<a id="live-convolution-transitions"></a>

### Live convolution transitions with worker ownership

A default-disabled ravet-graph feature hands worker-prepared native convolution engines or banks to audio through a bounded one-slot handoff, runs old and new engines through an explicit equal-gain or equal-power crossfade, returns old, refused and superseded engines for control-thread disposal and reports latency changes.

**Limits:** Feature convolution-transitions (optional ravet-signal). Convolver32/64 and ConvolutionBank32/64 only; fade 0..1048576 frames starting at block boundaries; two engines at most, the new one from empty history by default, so responses longer than the fade dip in level by up to the missing tail energy (optional priming in convolution-transition-continuity); mid-fade Refuse (stays refused under backpressure)/QueueOne/LatestWins (newest wins after the fade); latency RequireEqual or Report, unaligned by default (consumer applies host latency; mixed during fade; optional alignment in convolution-transition-continuity). Four returned slots plus one deferred slot, then a held completed outgoing; starts wait under backpressure; status authoritative, 16 best-effort reports with loss counts. Not a Processor; endpoints constructed/dropped off audio (the dropping thread frees its engines; the last endpoint frees queued engines). Offline exact-blend, allocation and concurrency evidence only; no deadline, DAW, device or platform claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-graph/src/convolution_transition.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/src/convolution_transition.rs), [`crates/ravet-graph/Cargo.toml`](../crates/ravet-graph/Cargo.toml).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-graph/tests/convolution_transition.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/tests/convolution_transition.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/audio-graphs.md`](../docs/audio-graphs.md), [`docs/decisions/0272-impulse-response-preparation-and-live-convolution-transitions.md`](../docs/decisions/0272-impulse-response-preparation-and-live-convolution-transitions.md).

<a id="convolution-transition-continuity"></a>

### History priming and latency alignment for convolution transitions

Optional continuity policies for live convolution transitions: a prepared input-history ring primes the incoming engine before its fade (single-block or bounded delayed-fade schedule) so it matches a never-switched engine, and prepared delay lines align engines of different latency during the fade, report each output-latency change and refuse differences above a configured maximum.

**Limits:** Feature convolution-transitions via convolution_transition_with_continuity; TransitionContinuity::NONE (default) is the same code path; its ADR 0272 behaviour is guarded by the 15 unchanged transition tests and by digests recorded from the ADR 0272 build in 108 scenarios. Priming history 1..1048576 frames per channel, frames_per_block >= history or > maximum_frames; delayed fades start within ceil((lag - B)/(B - block)) blocks; history shorter than the incoming tail only reduces the dip; a history shorter than requested primes only the recorded frames. Alignment maximum difference 0..1048576 frames, Release semantics only: the lower-latency path is delayed during the fade, the output latency changes at the start (increase, repeating the difference) or at fade completion (decrease, skipping it); without priming a delayed new path reads zeros for the first difference frames of the fade; a cut changes latency with no delay; no Hold mode, fractional latency or host negotiation. Refusal happens at the audio start boundary (returned as Refused with an AlignmentRefused event), not at offer. Continuity storage at most 256 MiB of samples, overflow-checked before fallible allocation; per-block copies are proportional to the block, and delay lines are forgotten in constant time at starts and reset (a delayed path reads zeros for its delay after reset). Offline exact-reference, impulse-onset, allocation and seeded concurrency evidence only; no deadline, DAW, device or platform claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-graph/src/convolution_transition.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/src/convolution_transition.rs), [`crates/ravet-graph/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/src/lib.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-graph/tests/convolution_transition_continuity.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/tests/convolution_transition_continuity.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/audio-graphs.md`](../docs/audio-graphs.md), [`docs/decisions/0275-convolution-transition-priming-and-latency-alignment.md`](../docs/decisions/0275-convolution-transition-priming-and-latency-alignment.md).

No antialias filtering, overshoot/alias/nonfinite/headroom/denormal caller policy; explicit sinc alternative. NaN sticky NaN, otherwise infinity sticky positive infinity until reset; no sanitization. No dependencies/allocation/framework locks/I/O; native sqrt/caller work unqualified for deadline/SIMD. Infinite ideal tail/no window RMS/true-peak/loudness/channel linking/lookahead/hysteresis/headroom repair/global denormal mode. Independent closed-form/convolution/wide-energy/native-release/rounding/partition/poison/all-channel/heap and actual native stereo Foundation/Graph gain evidence only; no physical/DAW/platform/acoustic support inference.
