## Prototype capabilities

<a id="embedded-reference-bridges"></a>

### Embedded gain and native Arduino processing subset

An allocation-free Rust stereo gain and caller-owned C ABI accompany a header-only C++11 stereo adapter/reference for Arduino cores without a Rust archive.

**Limits:** Immediate gain 0..4/default unity; Rust reference <=64 frames/eight events, C ABI block-start gain and <=128 samples. Native C++ stereo f32 timed parameters only, no arbitrary Rust DSP export. Matching C/Rust float ABI and pointer/exclusive lifetime obligations; explicit standalone panic policy. Arduino compile/link evidence only; no physical MCU/codec validation, audio-workload suitability or desktop gain parity.

<a id="extended-block-start-transport"></a>

### Extended block-start transport metadata

Optional portable details and checked bidirectional CLAP conversion preserve recording, active loop, pre-roll, signature, bar and tempo increment metadata.

**Limits:** Explicit details availability; CLAP cannot distinguish unknown/false status bits. Positive signature components, finite BPM/sample increment with tempo, bar with beats, active ordered loop bounds per known timeline. Native ingress ignores inactive loop fields; outgoing supplied inactive bounds reject. Sample/fixed-point rounding must preserve order. No extrapolation, DSP reset, mid-block updates or new DAW/device/deadline claim; offline macOS arm64 adapter evidence only.

<a id="prepared-audio-graphs"></a>

### Prepared acyclic processor routing

Owned portable f32/f64 nodes run in compiled topological order with channel mixing, parallel dry/wet routes, prepared latency compensation, bounded scratch and conservative tail declarations.

**Limits:** 128 nodes, 4096 connections, 65536 frames/path latency, 1024 input/output events per node, 64 MiB graph prepared audio/event storage. Later-node faults can leave preceding state advanced; explicit GraphStatus disables until reset. One selected native precision per graph; no implicit conversion, native discovery, GUI hosting or feedback cycles. Explicit filtered/generated event routes are a separate capability. Prepared whole-graph handoff is a separate capability.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-graph/Cargo.toml`](../crates/ravet-graph/Cargo.toml), [`crates/ravet-graph/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-graph/src/lib.rs).

<a id="buffered-graph-worker-device-output"></a>

### Buffered f32 graph-worker device output

A prepared no-input graph retains its audio-owner session on an explicit worker and publishes retained whole-frame queue suffixes; a separate output processor silences/counts underflow with live atomic diagnostics.

**Limits:** No-input f32 fixed blocks, 0..1024 explicit events per direction and zero aux buses; 1..64 matching channels and 1..65536 frames. Worker scratch<=32MiB and consumer scratch<=16MiB outside graph/native caps, plus queue memory. Explicit thread/wake/priming/rate matching/stream stop/worker join/main retirement. No clock/resampling/automatic recovery/audio input/edit/asynchronous event scheduler or deadline guarantee; reset preserves pending/queued audio. Loaded public silent sine and UMC1820/macOS arm64 20-channel 96kHz 10-second output observation; no long-session/drift/fault/deadline or broader platform/device support.

<a id="buffered-graph-worker-audio-input"></a>

### Queued audio input for native graph workers

Explicit matched input/output rings feed fixed f32 graph worker blocks, zero input shortages and preserve once-only input consumption through retained output publication.

**Limits:** 1..64 channels per direction, zero aux buses, fixed 1..65536 frames and graph 1024 event limit; combined worker scratch<=32MiB outside graph/native/queue caps. Outer malformed input/storage rejects before dequeue. Graph faults may consume input/advance histories, suppress faulty publication and retain error until reset without more drain; reset preserves queued/pending audio. Explicit rates/priming/wake/capture/stream stop/join/main retirement; no clock conversion/resampling/replay/physical capture/GUI/recovery/deadline claim. <a id="buffered-clocked-input-worker"></a>

An explicit worker reuses prepared sinc/FIFO clock correction to publish graph-rate f32 input, retaining destination suffixes without repeated capture consumption or conversion.

**Limits:** Matched 1..64 queue channels, nominal integer 8000..192000 rates and existing sinc ratio/correction bounds; raw capacity 2..65536 power-of-two with matching clock capacity/interior target, fixed 1..65536 frames. Output block<=16MiB additional to converter/internal/source/destination queues. Priming/underflow zeros and independent counters retain existing policy. Explicit capture/rates/wake/graph/events/shutdown/join; no reset/resampling-timestamp/physical clock alignment/stability/deadline/hotplug/platform claim. <a id="buffered-live-graph-worker"></a>

### Live prepared graph replacement in buffered workers

Already-prepared dynamic f32 graph engines share fixed worker input/output queues and consider live offers only after old audio suffixes publish, retaining main-owned retirement.

**Limits:** Exact prepared configuration, fixed graph 1024-event/worker32MiB limits; existing 1..4 handoff/retirement slots and separate per-graph/native memory budgets. Fresh renders return swap outcome, pending none; failed start/full retirement preserve old processing. Historical last_swap remains observable after processing faults. Fault latch/reset and once-only input/generated events remain. No reprepare/crossfade/tail drain/state migration/rate-layout-latency changes, GUI/event-generation/recovery scheduler or physical clock/device/deadline claim. Loaded two-instance public gain offline macOS arm64 evidence only.

Prepared main-bus adapters map 0..64 inputs/1..64 outputs at native f32/f64 precision, global parameters, selected-port short MIDI and validated block-start transport.

<a id="clap-auxiliary-buses"></a>

### Native CLAP auxiliary bus bridge

Native f32/f64 main and ordered auxiliary buses use independent compact input/output ports, complete input preflight and prepared sample/event storage.

**Limits:** Eight auxiliary buses, 64 channels per direction/bus, 65536 frames and 1024 input/output events each; combined samples/events cap 64 MiB. Exporters must advertise matching ports and precision. Existing gain/sine exports unchanged; separate sidechain reference records one REAPER mapping/render. General DAW auxiliary and other-format validation pending.

<a id="clap-generated-events"></a>

### Explicit bounded CLAP generated-event delivery

Native main-bus processing maps bounded physical parameter values/global gesture boundaries/modulation amounts and selected-port MIDI/normalized notes into core host events, with separate DSP/delivery status and explicit prefix rejection.

**Limits:** 1024 generated events; MIDI7 velocity quantization, reserved parameter ID/missing MIDI port rejects whole delivery. Host refusal discards suffix without audio rollback/retry. UMP packets map to CLAP MIDI2 with zero unused words; no pointer-based SysEx, CLAP note IDs/scoped modulation or other formats. Exporter modulation flags/DSP remain consumer policy. Prepared offline field/order/fault/heap fixtures pass; exported MIDI-output host evidence pending.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-clap/src/output.rs`](../crates/ravet-clap/src/output.rs), [`crates/ravet-clap/src/main_bus.rs`](../crates/ravet-clap/src/main_bus.rs).

<a id="exported-clap-native-performance-ports"></a>

### Explicit native CLAP performance ports in exported adapters

Selected native input/output ports preserve optional note IDs, unquantized f32 note velocity and all seven standard f64 expressions independently of raw MIDI/UMP routes.

**Limits:** Port indices 0..256; opt-in defaults retain MIDI output/native filtering. Exporter-owned CLAP dialect metadata/voice semantics. Concrete On channel/key; scoped Off/choke supported by the explicit native profile, while completion and scoped parameters use independent profiles. Unknown/unselected expression output/input filter; malformed selected input rejects pre-DSP with silence. Selected representable performance rejects at zero-frame process; flush input ignores performance, native performance output rejects whole delivery. Native IDs nonnegative i32; portable wider IDs reject before host prefix. Host refusal discards suffix without replay; rendered audio/DSP remain progressed. Offline adapter f32/f64/auxiliary evidence only, no new instrument/DAW/physical-device/deadline claim.

<a id="exported-clap-scoped-parameters"></a>

### Endpoint-scoped values and modulation in exported CLAP adapters

Distinct portable f64 scoped parameter events, independent native input/output selectors and explicit per-scope metadata flags preserve voice-target information without editing global state.

**Limits:** Finite full-f64 physical values/amounts, portable u32 IDs/native nonnegative i32; exact selected note input port 0..256, even all-wildcard targets remain port-scoped. Default input filters; malformed selected input rejects pre-DSP, raw exact all--1 alone is global. Whole generated missing routes/invalid IDs reject before prefix while successful audio/DSP remain progressed. Scoped parameter flush uses zero offsets, independently of performance flush policy. Empty cookies; exporter-owned range/voice precedence/base state/lifecycle. Metadata's eight scoped flags default false and enable no translation/DSP. Hosted metadata validation and instrument application separate; offline f32/f64/auxiliary adapter evidence only, no third-party/DAW/deadline claim.

Clack-backed preallocated scratch storage adapts mono/stereo f32 effects and global parameter values to the portable processor.

<a id="native-planar-processing-adapter"></a>

### Reusable native f32/f64 planar processor adaptation

SDK-independent prepared main/auxiliary scratch, checked raw bus pointers, complete typed event preflight and copied-input output rendering adapt exclusively borrowed portable processors to consumer native shims.

**Limits:** One main plus eight ordered auxiliaries, up to 64 channels per direction/bus, frames<=65536 and events<=1024 per direction; owned sample/generated-event payload<=64 MiB. Foreign live/aligned ranges and serialized lifecycle remain caller obligations. All inputs copy before outputs, output overlaps reject; zero frames permit null arrays. Exact supplied portable transport with consumer format validation. Faults silence supported declared prefixes/discard generated delivery without history rollback. Audio/reset panic poisons until fresh stopped preparation; normal heap evidence only, exceptional handlers may allocate. Consumer processor support, schemas/state C codecs, format-specific event/transport mappings, SDK registration/editor/delivery and native deadline remain separate; public Gain C ABI uses both precision paths.

<a id="owned-vst3-stopped-state"></a>

### Owned stopped VST3 component/controller state

An exact-table-paired companion captures owned opaque component/controller snapshots and applies bounded stopped state with explicit partial-failure poisoning and retained-stream lifetime.

**Limits:** Default-disabled vst3-catalogue and explicit caller-linked external SDK; main/exclusive stopped non-faulted child borrowing parent. Catalogue-v1/provider-v2 layouts unchanged; state companion32/record32/report24 on tested64bit macOS. Each explicit capture/source stream1..8MiB, keepers16/64MiB per core; whole range/shape/presence/UID preflight and capture publication, independent controller-component reader. Controller absent/NotImplemented/successful empty distinct. Opaque bytes do not authenticate version/schema/code. Success requires explicit reprepare; failed foreign compound restore or swallowed stream fault poisons processing without rollback but permits joined retirement/new-child recovery. Original returned SDK status/throw/stream diagnostic distinct; malformed restore reports fail closed. Frozen owned SDK streams retain host references; foreign release cannot cause final payload free, CONTROL reclaims. Retained streams force existing reserved-slot process pin even on failed/thrown getter, same-core v2 reopen and provider executable process lifetime; no unpin/static exit destruction. Controlled SDK-interface and actual Gain/Performance safe Rust capture/restore/render/controller rejection/recovery evidence only. No live restore, implicit restart/bus/parameter reconciliation, arbitrary third-party/DAW/editor/event/graph/other-platform or heap/RSS/deadline claim.

<a id="hosted-vst3-prepared-event-processing"></a>

### Prepared hosted VST3 events and block context

An exact-paired stopped catalogue and main-f32 audio companion copies selected buses/MIDI assignments, owns all input event payloads and publishes complete verified event/parameter output batches with independent native failure facts.

**Limits:** Trusted caller-linked native provider and plug-ins; 16 event buses/direction, 1..16 selected channels, 2048 events and 65536 payload bytes/direction, 64 output queues/2048 points. Main f32 mono/stereo effect or instrument only. 64MiB native event-pool keeper cap; observed six concurrently prepared children on the measured arm64 layout, about10.1MB event storage each plus parameter storage, separate from16 retained batches/child. Revised Rust wire tests and native fixtures are locally qualified; actual Gain mono/stereo and Performance SDK-image consumers pass through that revised owner against fresh W241 modules/canonical W227-243 archives. Core-owned controller-handler keepers, complete sibling numeric ownership protection and CONTROL exception provenance (R4) pass 98 native fixture commands and 31 CTest profiles. No DAW/platform/deadline support inference. Late native faults require stopped child retirement/recreation. Native f64/auxiliary buses and Graph ownership are the separate hosted-vst3-graph-banks record; editors are the separate hosted-vst3-editor-ownership record.

<a id="hosted-vst3-graph-banks"></a>

### Hosted VST3 native 32/64 aux buses and owned Graph banks

Default-disabled vst3-hosted-audio companion negotiates explicit main/aux bus profiles in native f32/f64, processes complete rich lanes through the scoped capability, and owns hosted children as canonical Graph processors retained by a bounded MAIN retirement registry.

**Limits:** Explicit unsafe exact-origin table/code/module trust; default-disabled vst3-hosted-audio feature (enables vst3-catalogue), no Cargo SDK link. Every advertised bus (<=16 per direction, <=1 main) needs an explicit active/inactive request; no defaultActive inference, fallback precision or layout substitution; <=64 packed active channels per direction, rate 0<r<=768000, frames 1..65536. Native refusals keep original stage/tresult; local refusal preserves the prior profile. f64 never narrowed. Graph bank consumes Library<'static>, 1..128 children, all prepared before the first lease begins, leases begin last with reverse unwind; MAIN registry 64 banks, nonwrapping generations, deliberately leaked, platform main thread on Apple. Node drop moves its bundle to a one-slot return ring; control drop only orphans; reclaim ends all leases before stop/retirement and never guesses a lease ended; forgotten nodes, refused returns and failed ends retain the bank. Rich lanes 1..4 batches/node, 64MiB per-bank budget, exact sequence/frames. Without a declared translation, framework events refuse; explicit translation is the separate hosted-vst3-graph-framework-events record. Checked reset refuses with RebuildRequired; fresh bank required. Evidence: mock-provider Rust unit/bank scenarios, 126 native fixture commands normal/fast-math, 61 CTest incl. actual W241 Gain/Performance, actual caller-linked Rust consumer debug/release (Gain mono/stereo f32/f64, Performance f32/f64, Graph Performance->Gain banks, orphaned control, 10000 blocks zero Rust allocations). Rust allocations only; foreign SDK/C++ heap, crash isolation, deadlines, DAW, third-party plug-ins and other platforms not claimed. No shared Sidechain VST3 module; Graph-bank child editors are not provided (scoped-instance editors are the hosted-vst3-editor-ownership record).

<a id="hosted-vst3-graph-framework-events"></a>

### Framework events in hosted VST3 Graph nodes

Opt-in per-node translation of ordinary RAVET parameter values, notes, note expression, poly pressure and block-start transport into hosted VST3 Graph-bank children, through declared parameter routes and scales, a selected note bus with an explicit note-ID policy, refuse/ignore policies and an explicit merge order with rich lanes.

**Limits:** Declared on MAIN with Vst3GraphBankBuilder::translate and checked against the refreshed catalogue before any lease begins; nodes without a translation still refuse framework events. Parameters: <=2048 declared routes (unique graph and native IDs, writable non-hidden native IDs), Normalized or declared Linear{minimum,maximum} scale, no inferred ID equality or plug-in mapping query, checked against a catalogue snapshot at build (no revalidation after a plug-in restart); exact-offset normalized points, no sorting or merging; same-ID same-offset Refuse (default) or opt-in LastWins (counted as ignored); <=64 distinct native IDs per block; bounded per-point admission (trailing equal-offset run and incremental 64-ID set); unmapped IDs Refuse or Ignore. Notes: one selected event input bus, Unidentified (-1) or RequireIdentified policy, NoteWithId 0..=i32::MAX, channel within the bus, velocity copied, tuning/length/ppqPosition/flags zero. Expressions (declared, not queried): volume /4, pan, tuning /240+0.5, vibrato, expression, brightness by note ID only (no channel/key); pressure as poly pressure with concrete channel/key, f32 narrowing. Transport: optional ProcessContext with flags exactly for present fields; playing and sample position required once anything is known; discontinuity, pre-roll, tempo increment, bar number and sample loops not represented. MIDI/UMP/modulation/gesture/scoped/choke/completion and undeclared capabilities follow Refuse or Ignore; ignored events are counted. Queued lanes: Refuse, FrameworkFirst or LaneFirst merge; two contexts refuse. <=2048 events and points per block, merged storage within the same limits, counted in the 64 MiB per-bank lane budget; AUDIO translation allocates, locks and frees nothing. Every refusal (including overflow) occurs before the plug-in runs, silences the block and returns ProcessStatus::Silence: neither the node nor an enclosing Graph latches, and GraphStatus does not carry the refusal. The reason is a distinct framework::Refusal, counted (refused), kept in a 16-record ring drained on MAIN (further details dropped, still counted), marked in diagnostics and, in queued mode, returned with the lane batch as Error::Framework. Native faults, admission refusals and events sent to untranslated nodes still fault and latch. No AUDIO panic path in translation. No IMidiMapping, output-event translation, note-ID synthesis or ppqPosition derivation. Evidence: Rust translator and mock-provider bank scenarios (exact offsets, every mapping and refusal with its exact reason, Graph-level refusal over seven blocks, 10000-cycle zero-allocation checks) and an actual caller-linked consumer over freshly built RAVET Gain and Performance VST3 bundles (f32/f64 nodes and a broadcast Graph chain against closed-form references, a refusing Gain node inside a Graph that continues with unity output and a later gain change, 10000 Graph blocks with zero Rust allocations), plus the VST3 native CMake/CTest suite. Local macOS arm64 only; Rust allocations only; no DAW, third-party plug-in, foreign-heap, deadline or other-platform claim.

<a id="hosted-vst3-editor-ownership"></a>

### Hosted VST3 editor ownership (macOS NSView)

Default-disabled vst3-editor companion creates a controller IPlugView on the main thread, attaches it to a caller-owned NSView, negotiates bounded sizes, handles IPlugFrame resize requests with explicit reentry policy, and releases the view before controller, component and module retirement.

**Limits:** macOS NSView only; explicit unsafe exact-origin table/code/module trust and unsafe caller-owned parent lifetime; default-disabled vst3-editor feature (enables vst3-catalogue), no Cargo SDK link. Accepted limitation: the Rust Editor exclusively borrows its Instance, so Rust-side scoped audio/prepare/start/stop/state calls need the editor closed; an open editor with running AUDIO is shown only through the raw native tables. mem::forget leaks the native editor, child and module (memory-safe). One editor per child; child destroy LIFECYCLE and module close CHILDREN while open. Owner replies carry an authoritative attached state (refusals included). Extents 1..16384; host resize needs canResize kResultTrue, checkSizeConstraint kResultTrue (== kResultOk; kResultFalse/kNotImplemented refuse, no fallback) with bounded rect and onSize kResultOk; recorded size re-queried by getSize. resizeView acknowledged during attached/setContentScaleFactor is applied later (after the call when attached, else at next attach) or counted as discarded; refused during other host view calls, off-main, foreign view, out of range, while detached, faulted or after teardown; idle requests apply onSize under the module busy flag and publish a one-slot consumer request cleared by detach, teardown and host resize. Content scale 0.25..8 optional, normally unsupported on macOS. No Rust callbacks or pointer escape. Evidence: injected SDK view fixture and substituted-loader provider fixture (normal/fast-math), C11 layout, Rust mock-provider tests, and the actual RAVET Gain VST3 editor in a hidden offscreen NSWindow (three cycles, one with concurrent audio through the native table); Performance/default Gain report unavailable. No DAW, third-party editor, visual, keyboard/focus, accessibility, edit-gesture adoption, Graph-bank child editor or other-platform claim.

<a id="auv3-async-host-owner"></a>

### Optional asynchronous AUv3 host ownership and joined main-bus audio

Default-disabled ravet-host au-hosting feature over a caller-linked authored macOS provider: explicit bounded registry catalogue, AUAudioUnit asynchronous instantiation with nonblocking main poll, observed-load-mode admission, stopped mono/stereo f32 main-bus preparation and joined scoped rendering through the public cached renderBlock.

**Limits:** macOS 12+ arm64 local evidence only; the caller links the native provider (no Cargo native link or build script). Explicit trusted native execution; catalogue 1..256, 16 process pending requests (cancelled requests hold capacity until real completion), 256 instances/reservations. Main-only !Send/!Sync owners and one Send/!Sync/non-Clone HRTB audio scope; joined return/unwind/forget end on main; failed end poisons and retains native ownership. Required load mode is checked against observed isLoadedInProcess; NSError domain/signed64 code stays separate from OSStatus and host status. One main output bus, zero or one matching input bus, mono/stereo planar f32, 0<rate<=768000Hz, 1..65536 frames; whole preflight, input capture before render, failures silence admitted prefixes and fault-close, tails retained, no retry or rollback. In-process evidence only: a test-process-registered public Gain and an injected SDK fault fixture; zero ordinary C++ new and zero Rust allocator requests over 2000 prepared calls each (Objective-C, Apple framework and libc allocation not counted). Actual out-of-process (IPC) rendering is unvalidated: a reviewed ad-hoc signed, non-/Applications registration was never discoverable. <a id="native-direct-audio-state"></a>

### Explicit native audio-owner complete state

An optional cache-paired companion applies fully validated physical global state and captures reordered complete snapshots on exclusively prepared native processors without control codecs or providers.

**Limits:** At most 1024 physical f32 fields/capacity; exact processor/cache/table/precision/library pairing and live aligned disjoint ranges are caller duties. Hooks require atomic failed restore and no heap actions, blocking or I/O. Panic shares DSP poison until fresh stopped prepare. Direct callbacks require no 64-bit atomics; live publication remains independently gated. No automatic generations/publication/scheduling/notifications/retry, consumer panic rollback, scoped/modulation/voice state, SDK factories or DAW/deadline claim. Repeated recall may restart smoothing; mixing protocols is explicit consumer policy.

<a id="native-prepared-telemetry"></a>

### Explicit prepared native telemetry

A separate consumer-selected native companion caches stable-ID readout metadata and revalidates complete physical f64 observations with exact u64 windows on exclusively prepared processors; Gain exposes its existing 12 meter fields.

**Limits:** At most 1024 descriptors/capacity with UTF-8 names255/units63, finite ordered display hints and known nonfinite-input flag. Raw finite f64 values preserve extremes/subnormals/signed zero and may exceed display hints. Exact cache/processor/table/precision/library and live aligned disjoint foreign ranges are caller obligations. Hook obeys no heap/blocking/I/O; snapshot panic shares DSP poison until fresh stopped prepare. No atomics required, implicit cross-thread observation/publication/UI-host scheduling, persistence/automation/events/clear, consumer panic rollback or DAW/deadline claim. Measurement/window/reset/retention and SDK display policy belong to consumers.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-native/src/telemetry.rs`](../crates/ravet-native/src/telemetry.rs), [`crates/ravet-native/include/RavetNativeTelemetry.h`](../crates/ravet-native/include/RavetNativeTelemetry.h), [`examples/gain-native/src/lib.rs`](../examples/gain-native/src/lib.rs).

<a id="native-cpp-processor-client"></a>

### Reusable native C++ client and SDK reference adoption

An SDK-independent C++17 owner composes native lifecycle, optional explicit state and telemetry caches; the Gain VST3 processor consumes it with tagged events and retained controller/program/editor protocols.

**Limits:** Exact v1 shapes/required callbacks/precision/counts/originating core addresses; control acquisition/preparation/retirement, exclusive DSP callbacks and shared cached metadata. Selected state and telemetry companions require the exact supplied core pointer; byte-identical copied core tables reject before any resource creator. Violating CONTROL acquisition/query exceptions balance already acquired resources; native ABI/destruction remain nonthrowing obligations, with no arbitrary foreign-code authentication. Exact types/library and live aligned disjoint ranges remain caller duties. No copy/move, fallback, hidden state/mailbox/codecs, automatic publication/scheduling/retry, generic SDK factories/editor/buses, performance/scoped/transport/generated-event mapping or DAW/deadline/platform/signing claim. Native callback poison/result/silence semantics and consumer 31-bit generation/measurement/display policies remain explicit.

<a id="native-client-exact-acquisition"></a>

### Exact native client origin and balanced acquisition

C++ native client admits exact originating state/telemetry core tables with whole CONTROL preflight and balanced partial acquisition.

**Limits:** C++ behavior change rejects callback-equivalent copied core tables; trusted library/table lifetimes and nonthrowing native ABI remain caller obligations. CONTROL acquisition exception cleanup is defensive only. Existing Gain32/64 actual archive normal/fast tests are local, not DAW/device/deadline validation. Public rebuild/format qualification pending.

<a id="vst3-block-start-transport"></a>

### Explicit VST3 block-start transport mapping

An external-SDK C++17 helper requests/maps canonical available sample/musical positions, tempo, signature and playback/details into native transport; Gain forwards it before pending state or processing.

**Limits:** Null means unknown. Finite positive SDK rate/tempo, finite advertised music/cycles, positive u16 signatures; exact i64/f64 and used signed zero preserved. Active ordered cycle bounds require known musical position for native v1; inactive/positionless bounds omitted with loop state retained. Bar start without exact bar number, system/continuous time, SMPTE/frame rate, clock/chord, increments/sample loops/discontinuity/pre-roll are unmapped. Unknown/unavailable/unmapped fields ignored; no invented availability/reset/extrapolation/rounding, transport-driven Gain DSP, DAW timeline/deadline/platform/signing claim. Live aligned context/output/library remain caller duties; normal framework mapping has no callbacks/heap/locks/I/O.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-native/include/RavetVst3Transport.hpp`](../crates/ravet-native/include/RavetVst3Transport.hpp), [`crates/ravet-native/include/RavetNativeScalars.hpp`](../crates/ravet-native/include/RavetNativeScalars.hpp), [`examples/gain-vst3/src/gain.cpp`](../examples/gain-vst3/src/gain.cpp).

<a id="vst3-native-performance-input"></a>

### Explicit VST3 native performance input

An external-SDK C++17 helper maps selected-bus notes, poly pressure and six standard note expressions into canonical native records after complete bounded event-list validation.

**Limits:** At most1024 raw/expanded events and65536 frames; ordered offsets/ties/zero-frame rules, single getter reads,56KiB bounded stack scratch. SDK int32 IDs preserve all bits except absent-1; unquantized f32 velocity, cents to semitone tuning expansion, normalized volume*4/tuning240*(x-.5), exact other f64 expression values. Unknown expressions reject by default or explicitly filter after scalar/ID validation; other selected SDK types reject. Nonselected payloads filter after header/timing/order validation. Optional length/ppq/flags unrepresented; no voice matching, SDK instrument export/controller advertisement, output event delivery, SysEx/text/int expressions or DAW/deadline/platform claim. Visitor refusal retains its prior effects; stage privately before DSP/state/host publication.

<a id="vst3-native-performance-output"></a>

### Explicit VST3 native performance output

An external-SDK C++17 helper maps representable canonical native notes and expressions into selected-bus SDK output, preflighting the complete stream and reporting exact host-prefix refusal.

**Limits:** At most1024 records/65536 frames; bounded1024-SDK-event stack scratch, ordered offsets/ties/zero-frame rules. Concrete/scoped-concrete Off and pressure require exact widened f32; standard expressions require ID-only scope, all int32 identity bits except reserved-1. Volume/4 is exact or rejects subnormal rounding/underflow; tuning/240+.5 is explicit floating unit arithmetic with possible rounding. No wildcard/precision loss, choke/end masquerade, implicit MIDI/UMP/SysEx/parameters/text/int conversion or inferred ppq/flags/length. Whole invalid output rejects before host calls; refusal retains accepted prefix/DSP and discards suffix without rollback/replay/retry. Gain has no performance output and does not adopt helper; no SDK instrument/DAW/deadline/platform claim.

<a id="vst3-native-audio-buses"></a>

### Prepared VST3 native audio bus mapping

An external-SDK C++17 fixed profile maps logical native main/auxiliary buses into independent compact SDK directions at native f32/f64, with complete shape/range/output-overlap preflight and bounded fault silence; Gain adopts it.

**Limits:** Native config1..9 nonempty buses,0..64 channels per direction/576 total,1..65536 frames and up to 1024 events; failed control configure retains prior profile and does not prepare DSP. Fixed profile rejects host count/channel/precision mismatch; zero-frame fully omitted or exact metadata accepted, sample arrays ignored. Positive frames require all pointers even when silence flagged. Inputs may alias outputs across buses; output active ranges must be disjoint, aligned and nonoverflowing. Bounded sorted output ranges; no heap/locks/I/O in normal mapping. Foreign live metadata/array/sample ownership and writable metadata exclusions remain caller duty. Fault cleanup touches supported exact output shapes/frame/precision only, skips invalid sample pointers, retains tails and sets exact cleared flags. Generic SDK bus registration/speaker arrangements/factory/DAW/deadline/platform evidence remains separate; Gain retains mono/stereo effect layouts.

<a id="vst3-cached-parameter-input"></a>

### Prepared VST3 cached global parameter input

Optional external-SDK helpers use precision-matched native caches and validate/copy all raw global queue points before a prepared visitor; Gain uses them for mapped automation with retained program expansion and stable merging.

**Limits:** Control creation/retirement, exact table/cache/library and borrowed host lifetime; <=1024 targets/queues/total points and <=65536 frames, <=16KiB raw scratch. Reserved/duplicate targets reject; explicit readonly/routing policy, global normalized f64 intent narrows to f32. Single point read, full raw/unknown value/timing/capacity validation before visitor, referenced-memory IEEE checks for fast-math. Visitor failure may retain private scratch effects; publish state/output/DSP only after success. No framework heap/providers/locks/I/O on cached/validation paths; host/visitor obligations remain. No continuous curve interpolation, gestures/scoped/performance/transport, generic factory/output/scheduling or additional host/platform/deadline claim.

Version-one native records preserve every portable event kind with full identities/scoped f64 values, canonical fields and atomic bounded conversion into prepared storage; Gain shares the legacy global parameter decoder.

**Limits:** In-process native layout only, not wire/preset serialization or SDK registration. At most 1024 events; exact widened f32 scalars required for global controls/velocities. <a id="native-transport-record-codec"></a>

### Exact C-layout native transport snapshots

Independent native availability/flags preserve exact block-start positions, tempo and extended transport while validating semantic dependencies and canonical fields without allocation.

**Limits:** In-process v1 record only; no wire serialization, fixed-point conversion, extrapolation or automatic reset. Finite beat/bar values and positive finite tempo, increment requires tempo, bar requires beats, active ordered loop bounds require their timeline, nonzero u16 signatures. Consumers decode before DSP and own foreign rejection/silence and SDK mapping. Direct typed adapter pass-through stays unchanged. No additional DAW/platform/deadline claim.

<a id="explicit-clap-hosting"></a>

### Explicit CLAP discovery and trusted catalogues

Bounded explicit non-loading candidate scans and trusted native entry loading provide owned byte-preserving plugin metadata and live-instance library retention through Clack.

**Limits:** 32 directories/4096 entries/1024 candidates, 1024 plugins and bounded descriptor strings/features. No recursion/system scan, sandbox, signing check, crash timeout, automatic host callbacks/device/GUI or other formats. Native upstream Clack gain and RAVET gain/sine catalogue/state/three-block f32 lifecycles pass locally; broad compatibility pending.

<a id="guarded-clap-editor-hosting"></a>

### Guarded trusted CLAP editor hosting

A main-thread instance-borrowing guard owns negotiated editor creation, embedded parent attachment, bounded resizing, idempotent show/hide and guaranteed paired destruction.

**Limits:** Embedded sizes 1..16384 per dimension; native parent attachment/transient lifetime is an explicit unsafe caller contract. No parent window creation/pump, host GUI request scheduling, focus/scale policy or device integration. Local Cocoa RAVET/upstream EGUI child/lifecycle fixtures pass; visual hide/accessibility, floating/other OS APIs and broad compatibility unvalidated.

<a id="parameter-gesture-event-routing"></a>

### Explicit global parameter gesture boundaries

Typed stable-ID begin/end events cross parameter graph filters and complete worker queues, map to generated CLAP output and optionally map from hosted native graph output.

**Limits:** Raw boundaries only; no scalar state change, pairing/ownership/cancellation/recording policy. Hosted output requires explicit writable parameter mapping and opt-in; disabled/unmapped filters, read-only/offset/order/capacity rejects with nonrollback block failure. Zero-frame parameter flush permits offset zero. Shared graph 1024 and native slot limits; no native input translation, GUI scheduler, other-format or host automation-recording claim. Loaded public f32/f64 fixture macOS arm64 evidence only.

<a id="clap-parameter-gesture-input"></a>

### Explicit CLAP parameter gesture input

Opt-in native begin/end translation and mapped hosted native input preserve raw boundaries alongside parameter values without automatic state edits or pairing.

**Limits:** Default ingress ignores native boundaries; default hosted input rejects portable boundaries. Explicit hosted writable input map required before activation; disabled/unknown input rejects before native mutation. Shared prepared capacities and process timing; flush ingress offsets normalize to zero, portable empty blocks require zero. <a id="global-parameter-modulation-events"></a>

### Explicit global parameter modulation signals

Finite signed physical modulation amounts remain separate from base values across graph filters/worker queues, opt-in CLAP input translation and generated global CLAP output.

**Limits:** Finite f32 physical amounts; no automatic base-value change, combination/clipping/smoothing/reset/persistence or per-note scope. CLAP input defaults to ignored modulation, explicitly enabled global amounts must narrow to finite f32; scoped events ignore, invalid whole input rejects before DSP, flush offsets normalize to zero. Output preserves representability preflight/host prefix refusal. No synthesized native metadata flags, reference plug-in support, native hosting/other-format/host/device/deadline claim. Existing graph/queue/bridge bounds apply.

<a id="hosted-clap-global-parameter-modulation"></a>

### Mapped native global modulation in hosted nodes

Independent builder input/output opt-ins map finite global physical modulation through cached writable native modulatable identities, with reusable explicit CLAP metadata registration.

**Limits:** Explicit direction mappings, default disabled; 4096 native shared slots versus graph 1024 cap. Input finite f32 widens to f64 and unsupported targets reject before native mutation. Enabled global output requires writable modulatable metadata and finite f32 narrowing; disabled/unmapped/scoped filters, selected data/order/offset/capacity faults clear block with nonrollback BackendFailure. Scalar base range/step checks stay separate; zero-frame flush supported. No cookies/rescan/modulation matrix/per-note/other-format/crash isolation or host/device/deadline claim. Public synthetic f32/f64 macOS arm64 evidence only.

<a id="hosted-clap-scoped-parameters"></a>

### Mapped scoped values and modulation in hosted CLAP graphs

Explicit mapped native graph directions validate cached scope metadata and preserve full f64 parameter values/modulation, selected input-port voice scope and zero-time flush separately from global state.

**Limits:** Selected CLAP note input endpoint plus explicit maps/nonzero shared capacities; writable input/output scoped metadata. Most-specific supplied ID/key/channel/port requires its corresponding automation/modulation flag, independently of global flags. Portable u32/native nonnegative i32; finite f64 values within native range/steps, signed finite modulation independent of base bounds/steps. Disabled/invalid input rejects whole prefix pre-native. Unknown IDs/unselected or wildcard ports filter; selected output metadata/scalar/timing/capacity faults discard complete portable output without native rollback. Raw exact all--1 alone is global; empty input cookies/owned private storage. Metadata changes require retirement/reprepare. No voice allocation/state migration/GUI/recording or third-party/DAW/deadline claim; linked offline f32/f64 fixture evidence only.

<a id="hosted-clap-note-identities"></a>

### Explicit note identities in hosted CLAP graphs

Portable identified On/Off events and opt-in selected native CLAP routes preserve concrete note IDs, timing and velocity without inferred voice policy.

**Limits:** Portable u32 identities; native0..i32::MAX with explicitly selected CLAP note ports per enabled direction. Default input rejects, output filters specific IDs; wildcard native notes retain legacy events. Invalid input rejects whole prefix pre-native; selected raw native IDs<-1 reject rather than normalize. No identity-loss MIDI/MPE/UMP/generated-MIDI conversion, voice allocation/lifetime, choke/end/per-note parameter or new third-party/DAW/deadline claim. Offline portable/queue/unit and linked f32/f64 fixture evidence only.

<a id="scoped-clap-note-expressions"></a>

### Scoped standard note expressions in hosted CLAP graphs

Portable wildcard channel/key/ID targets and opt-in selected native routes preserve seven standard expression kinds with full f64 values.

**Limits:** Finite standard ranges; portable volume0..4, CLAP strictly positive0<x<=4 rejects mute rather than clamp. Portable u32 IDs/native nonnegative i32; exact selected CLAP port per enabled direction. Default input rejects, output filters expressions. Disabled/invalid input rejects whole prefix before native mutation; unknown types/other or wildcard ports filter; selected malformed output faults without native rollback. Default generated MIDI output rejects whole expression streams before delivery. No voice application/allocator, lifecycle/per-note parameters, loss to MIDI/MPE/UMP or third-party/DAW/deadline claim; offline linked f32/f64 ABI evidence only.

<a id="scoped-note-release-choke"></a>

### Scoped note release and choke

Portable wildcard targets carry key release velocity and scalar-free choke through graph queues and selected hosted/exported native CLAP routes.

**Limits:** Finite Off velocity 0..1, portable u32 IDs/native nonnegative i32; receiver-owned voice matching/release/termination. Hosted flags default false and require selected CLAP directions; invalid/disabled input rejects whole prefixes pre-native, default/unselected output filters. Native wildcard-channel/key Off preserves scope; concrete output Off retains legacy/identity profile. Raw negative scope rejects rather than normalize; native choke velocity ignored. Selected output faults retain native history; zero-frame/flush performance restrictions remain. Generated MIDI rejects whole scoped streams before prefix. No note-end completion, implicit MIDI/MPE/UMP conversion, public instrument behavior or third-party/DAW/hardware/deadline claim; offline linked f32/f64 evidence only.

<a id="note-completion-notifications"></a>

### Directional note completion notifications

Portable completion targets, graph/queue preservation and opt-in native profiles notify controllers on originating note input endpoints independently of release/choke and performance output.

**Limits:** Checked channel/key/wildcard/u32 portable scope and native nonnegative i32 IDs. Carrier offsets order delivery without voice termination times. Hosted explicit CLAP input route/nonzero capacities; native timestamp/velocity ignored, canonical offset uses previous retained offset or zero. Disabled/unselected/wildcard ports filter; selected raw scope/capacity faults discard portable output without native rollback. Portable hosted input rejects whole prefixes. Exported independent input-endpoint output selector below 256, whole missing-route/width/flush rejection before host prefix with audio progressed; incoming native completions filter under generic timing validation. No automatic completion/allocator/ID reuse, MIDI conversion, public reference behavior or third-party/DAW/deadline claim; synthetic offline evidence only.

<a id="sample-timed-ump"></a>

### Sample-timed UMP and CLAP packet routing

Framed UMP portable events preserve ordered sample offsets and map to/from selected-port CLAP MIDI2 events without resolution conversion.

**Limits:** Packet transport only; processors own semantic validation and negotiated protocol. Existing reference processors advertise MIDI 1.0 only. No MIDI 2 DAW/device performance claim, pointer-based SysEx mapping, protocol negotiation or automatic synthesis conversion.

<a id="midi-device-packets"></a>

### Explicit MIDI devices and bounded complete packets

Native midir connections enumerate/select exact ports, receive short/SysEx packets through prepared SPSC storage and send validated packets to explicit destinations.

**Limits:** 1024-byte complete packets, power-of-two 1..1024 slots; newest full input drops. Connection-local microsecond timestamps require explicit audio mapping. No fragmented SysEx, UMP, automatic reconnect/hotplug, physical-device or non-macOS runtime/deadline claim.

<a id="core-midi-ump-endpoints"></a>

### Guarded macOS CoreMIDI UMP endpoints

Exact-ID protocol-selected native inputs/outputs and owned virtual destinations/sources connect bounded exact-word UMP handoff through guarded native callback lifetime.

**Limits:** macOS/Xcode backend only, runtime scope macOS 27.0.1 arm64. 4096 endpoints/packet queue, 1023-byte display names, 1024 native packets/4096 words per callback. Handles thread-local; close waits outside callbacks. Native conversion/host-tick clock explicit; physical devices, negotiation/hotplug/deadlines and other OS backends unvalidated.

<a id="standalone-output-devices"></a>

### Standalone output audio devices

Explicit CPAL enumeration/ID selection and configured f32 output streams adapt owned prepared processors through bounded planar scratch; a CLI runs silent callback validation.

**Limits:** Output-only, 1..64 channels and at most 65,536 scratch frames; no inputs, auxiliary buses, MIDI/events, implicit resampling/conversion, hotplug subscriptions or automatic recovery. macOS UMC1820 20-channel 96 kHz silent callbacks exercised; audible output, latency, deadlines and other targets remain unvalidated.

<a id="input-duplex-devices"></a>

### Input capture and FIFO duplex effects

Explicit CPAL f32 input streams publish whole-frame prefixes to a prepared ring; duplex rendering zero-fills underflow, partitions variable callbacks and feeds portable effects.

**Limits:** 1..64 channels per direction, power-of-two ring 1..65536 frames, scratch up to 65536. Matching nominal rates, independently clocked/sequential streams; no drift compensation or sample-exact alignment. No automatic recovery, hotplug or MIDI/events; hidden-producer automatic recording integration is exercised synthetically, without physical recording validation.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-device/src/input.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/input.rs), [`crates/ravet-device/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/lib.rs), [`tools/device-probe/src/main.rs`](../tools/device-probe/src/main.rs).

<a id="explicit-output-recovery"></a>

### Caller-scheduled exact-device output recovery

An explicit control-thread owner preserves healthy f32 output, releases missing/failed streams and prepares/starts fresh DSP through a caller-supplied factory.

**Limits:** Exact host-local ID 1..4096 bytes/no NUL, fixed existing f32 config/scratch limits; no fallback/settings mutation/timer/hotplug subscription/state migration/clock compensation/duplex or native plugin scheduling. Backend work can block; errors retry only on service. Controlled transitions and UMC1820 silent manual restart evidence, physical unplug/real backend fault/other-platform/deadline unvalidated.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-device/src/recovery.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/recovery.rs), [`crates/ravet-device/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/lib.rs), [`tools/device-probe/src/main.rs`](../tools/device-probe/src/main.rs).

<a id="explicit-duplex-recovery"></a>

### Caller-scheduled exact-pair duplex recovery

An explicit control-thread owner releases both streams when either exact device disappears or either backend fails, reopening fresh FIFO/DSP through a caller factory.

**Limits:** Fixed f32 1..64-channel matching-rate configs, scratch 1..65536, power-of-two ring 1..65536; exact IDs 1..4096 bytes/no NUL. No fallback/settings mutation/timer/hotplug subscription/state migration/clock compensation/recording or native plugin scheduling. Controlled transitions and silent UMC1820 manual pair restarts only; physical removal/real backend failure/drift/other-platform/deadline unvalidated.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-device/src/recovery.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/recovery.rs), [`crates/ravet-device/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/lib.rs), [`tools/device-probe/src/main.rs`](../tools/device-probe/src/main.rs).

**Tests:** [`crates/ravet-device/src/recovery.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/recovery.rs), [`crates/ravet-device/tests/input.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/tests/input.rs), [`tools/device-probe/src/main.rs`](../tools/device-probe/src/main.rs).

**Documentation:** [`docs/audio-devices.md`](../docs/audio-devices.md), [`docs/decisions/0091-explicit-duplex-recovery.md`](../docs/decisions/0091-explicit-duplex-recovery.md).

<a id="reclaimable-clocked-duplex"></a>

### Explicit paired clocked callback retirement and original-owner recovery

An additive f32 paired CPAL route retains the unique prepared clocked renderer and matching capture endpoints until all four callbacks retire, then allows stopped file/DSP extraction and explicit owner-preserving recovery.

**Limits:** No new dependency/defaults; existing clocked rate/channel/ring/frame/corrected-sinc profile. Failure-owned prepared constructors preserve original P/raw consumer; fallible scratch before child prepare; legacy consuming signatures unchanged, failed-prepare inactive contract. One control retirement worker; disjoint private UnsafeCell capture/renderer, unique non-Clone FnMut data guards, two atomic-only error guards, no Weak/public clones. All FOUR Acquire retirement flags plus stable sole strong ownership before extraction; callback Arc field Drop cannot be inferred from flags. Framework capture Drop only publishes flag/releases non-last Arc; no producer/consumer/DSP/scratch/counter disposal there, including early receiver Drop/asynchronous native owners. Native CPAL/OS locks/closure allocation/destructors and panic runtime remain separate limits. Nonblocking poll; explicit CONTROL wait without deadline/cancellation. Original spawn/input/output/preparation/start errors retain Immediate/Pending ownership, no hidden retry. Caught polling fault returns exclusive stopped owner; foreign lifecycle/restore panic may lose recovery, no forged receipt. Capture/output panic disables its guard, histories exceptional. Stopped result exposes no render/mutable child and consumes into original P and matching raw consumer/PreparedCapture, once-only deactivate; converted/prefetched histories discarded CONTROL, queued raw cursor unchanged. Explicit selected-ID recovery Owned/Live/Retiring/Disabled, known live callback faults retire before selection, healthy selection errors retain pair/original error without absence inference; no enumerate/open/restore while pending or disabled; after proof restore original P/receipt before fresh pair. Normal restore errors retain actual mutated P/receipt; successful restore once, failed opens preserve ownership, generation advances only after successful start. No automatic timer/fallback/subscription/state migration; ordinary DSP faults explicit reset/reopen policy. All24 Drop orders, actual concurrent capture/render and Wave/IntegerSinc/indexed-worker/W215 stopped failed/successful seek17/reprepare/exact suffix/drain qualified offline. Two short silent paired CoreAudio cycles on one USB interface prove original-owner retirement/reopen only; no acoustic validation, synchronized starts, timestamp alignment, live mailbox, physical hotplug/drift, long-session latency, callback/teardown deadline or broad device/platform claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-device/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/lib.rs), [`crates/ravet-device/src/input.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/input.rs), [`crates/ravet-device/src/clocked.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/clocked.rs), [`crates/ravet-device/src/reclaimable_clocked.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/reclaimable_clocked.rs), [`crates/ravet-device/src/reclaimable_clocked_recovery.rs`](../crates/ravet-device/src/reclaimable_clocked_recovery.rs).

<a id="native-web-editor"></a>

### Native web editor backends

Local HTML editors use Cocoa/WebKit, Windows HWND/WebView2 or Linux X11/WebKitGTK with finite backing colours, bounded JSON messages, coalesced snapshots and explicit teardown. Cocoa editor views accept initial drags from inactive windows. WebKit browser context menus are suppressed in all frames while consumer right-click actions still receive events.

**Limits:** C++ API on all three platforms; the separate Cargo Rust binding remains macOS only. Caller owns the UI loop and callback lifetime. Linux requires GTK3 X11/XWayland, WebKitGTK 4.1 >=2.40 and UI-thread GLib pumping; an existing Wayland GTK context is rejected. Loaded SWELL hosts must provide cooperative LOAD_GTK initialization or editor creation is rejected. Windows requires the WebView2 loader and installed runtime; creation is asynchronous. 50 ms polling, one evaluation in flight, 65,536-byte JSON and 1 MiB inline HTML limits. WebKit context-menu suppression has no native opt-out; macOS synthetic DOM evidence only, Linux runtime validation pending. Windows context-menu policy is unchanged. Linux software painting is selectable with RAVET_WEB_LINUX_SOFTWARE_RENDERING (default OFF); UI CPU cost is unmeasured. Linux lifecycle evidence in local Ubuntu containers and native Omarchy/XWayland, Windows compile evidence only, macOS native probes; no DAW or deadline support claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-surface/native/RavetWebView.h`](../crates/ravet-surface/native/RavetWebView.h), [`crates/ravet-surface/native/RavetWebView.mm`](../crates/ravet-surface/native/RavetWebView.mm), [`crates/ravet-surface/native/RavetWebViewLinux.cpp`](../crates/ravet-surface/native/RavetWebViewLinux.cpp), [`crates/ravet-surface/native/RavetWebViewWindows.cpp`](../crates/ravet-surface/native/RavetWebViewWindows.cpp), [`crates/ravet-surface/native/mingw/EventToken.h`](../crates/ravet-surface/native/mingw/EventToken.h), [`crates/ravet-surface/native/CMakeLists.txt`](../crates/ravet-surface/native/CMakeLists.txt).

<a id="native-editor-binding"></a>

### Cargo macOS WebKit ownership binding

An explicit native crate builds Cocoa/WebKit through Xcode, checks main-thread creation, owns view and callback context, copies bounded snapshots and destroys native callback machinery before releasing state.

**Limits:** macOS only; Xcode build host required, native deployment target 12. View is not Send/Sync; caller supplies run loop and a valid live NSView parent through a documented unsafe attach. macOS owned-view resizing is available. No portable widgets, x86_64/macOS-12 runtime, native heap or DAW support claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-webview/src/lib.rs`](../crates/ravet-webview/src/lib.rs), [`crates/ravet-webview/src/macos.rs`](../crates/ravet-webview/src/macos.rs), [`crates/ravet-webview/build.rs`](../crates/ravet-webview/build.rs).

<a id="native-editor-c-abi"></a>

### Rust-owned macOS editor C ABI

Native consumers create/attach/resize/show/destroy Rust-owned WebViews with counted UTF-8 callbacks, UI-thread status checks and retained exactly-once foreign-context release.

**Limits:** macOS/Xcode only; trusted HTML 1 MiB, snapshot 65536 bytes, dimensions <=16384. Consumers provide valid live handles/buffers/NSView parents and nonthrowing callbacks; host owns window/run loop. Wrong-thread destroy retains ownership; accepted destroy consumes. No format/product policy, other-OS/assistive-tech/DAW support claim.

<a id="standalone-settings-popup"></a>

### Default standalone Audio/MIDI settings popup

Reusable main-thread standalone windows resize their embedded page with native content and include a native title-bar settings button and standard device/channel-pair/rate/buffer/MIDI checklist popup with persistent exact device selections by default, with explicit full opt-out.

**Limits:** macOS 12+ Cocoa/WebKit and Xcode tools. Trusted local inline HTML up to 1 MiB with one closing body tag, reserved DOM IDs and control-thread snapshot/action contract. Consumer owns device inventory/validation/routing/lifecycle; creation opens no devices. Optional initial content aspect-ratio lock; programmatic resize fits the requested rectangle and native minimum size applies. Versioned preferences up to 8 KiB use a stable window-title key; hidden fixtures use process-local memory. Missing devices are unselected, restored settings never start audio. Plug-in editors and headless fixtures retain their own host/window policy. Programmatic native UI evidence, no broader platform or assistive-technology claim.

**Source:** [`crates/ravet-webview/src/standalone.rs`](../crates/ravet-webview/src/standalone.rs), [`crates/ravet-webview/native/StandaloneWindow.mm`](../crates/ravet-webview/native/StandaloneWindow.mm), [`crates/ravet-webview/web/io-settings.html`](../crates/ravet-webview/web/io-settings.html).

<a id="reusable-web-controls"></a>

### Reusable local web controls

Shared slider/number, linear/logarithmic rotary knob, polyphonic piano keyboard, toggle, choice, action-button and meter components provide explicit gestures/actions, held-key ownership, nonfeedback host refresh and retryable disposal; piano chords/glissando share lifecycle release, disabled keys remain opaque and meter text retains actual overload levels. Shared styles prevent UI label/body text selection while keeping editable fields and code output selectable. Knob and slider/fader pointer gestures leave numeric editing, suppress label activation and pointer focus outlines, and preserve direct number entry and keyboard focus styling.

**Limits:** Trusted inline documents up to 1 MiB; physical slider/knob values with optional logarithmic knob travel, 256 choices and 32-bit IDs. Meter labels 256 and formatter text 4096 JavaScript units; finite nonnegative readings. Consumer owns DOM labels/layout/theme, host schema/queue policy and asynchronous errors. Piano note bounds 0..127 with white endpoints and up to 128 external notes. Native macOS WebKit programmatic and browser keyboard evidence; no assistive-tech audit or complete native widget toolkit/platform claim.

An explicit surface open-file API owns its completion callback, supports a native parent and extension filter, and returns cancellation without any product file policy.

<a id="clap-editor-control"></a>

### CLAP editor control and gesture bridge

A main-thread gain/bypass edit API queues complete edits and continuous begin/value/end gestures, retains partial host output progress, invalidates stale edits after restore, and exposes coherent requested values and coalesced meters.

**Limits:** 32 queued commands/complete edits and at most 96 drain iterations per callback, also used by the macOS embedded gain editor. One continuous gesture at a time; live updates reserve end capacity and reject overflow. REAPER 7.82/macOS arm64 GUI gain recording exercised; no guaranteed host delivery. CLAP must serialize consumers; generation must not wrap across outstanding edits.

<a id="runtime-native-abi"></a>

### Rust runtime native ownership facade

Opaque handles, bounded returned buffers and consumed callback contexts expose Rust runtime APIs to native SDK consumers; narrow Rust OS bindings supply module paths, macOS UUID and Windows SMBIOS inputs.

**Limits:** Foreign callers guarantee pointer validity, nonthrowing callbacks and serialized teardown. C++ convenience read maps errors to empty text; Rust/C status retain errors. macOS arm64/Omarchy x64 ABI tests and native facade probes; private macOS consumer integration, Windows runtime validation pending. Raw hardware queries include no product hashing or transmission.

**Limits:** macOS arm64 validator/smoke-host and REAPER 7.82 session, automation and render evidence. Default macOS native-editor feature provides an embedded Cocoa gain GUI, committed and continuous gestures and coalesced meters. No broader host or production compatibility claim.

<a id="auv3-native-adapter"></a>

### Native AUv3 processor and parameter editor

A paired f32 native processor/state entry renders through AUAudioUnit with physical global parameters, timed changes/continuing ramps, host bypass, complete live state, transport and opt-in MIDI/UMP input, plus a native parameter editor and embedded extension fixture.

**Limits:** One main bus, up to 128 parameters/64 channels per direction, public mono/stereo Gain; bounded 1024 links and 1024 minus parameter-count flattened events. macOS arm64 and iOS simulator in-process evidence; no extension discovery/IPC, DAW, physical device, production signing or deadline claim. An explicit AVAudioEngine/AVAudioSession owner hosts a native effect with microphone permission, preferred device settings, interruption/route/reset rebuilding, retained state and selected CoreMIDI input; the public iOS/iPadOS Gain app exposes native Audio/MIDI settings and consumer-selected deployment minimums.

<a id="android-mobile-standalone"></a>

### Android standalone audio and MIDI host

An explicit AAudio f32 effect owner provides prepared planar conversion/chunking, nonblocking capture reads with shortage silence/counters, atomic error handoff, stopped retirement and a bounded immediate MIDI queue; the public foreground app exposes permission/audio-focus and Audio/MIDI settings, with consumer-selected minimum API, compile/target SDK and build-tools.

Equal input/output rates/channels, no clock drift conversion; Gain mono/stereo, immediate MIDI 1 input, explicit Start recovery, no SysEx/MIDI 2/background audio or persisted app sessions.

<a id="auv2-performance-instrument"></a>

### Public AUv2 native performance instrument bundle

Public mono/stereo native performance AUv2 instrument adopts selected planar f32/f64 audio, timed MIDI and Level intent, coherent Level state, and checked stopped/offline/reset lifecycle over reusable AU helpers.

**Limits:** External Apple AudioUnit SDK, macOS arm64 local in-process evidence. Explicit packed float32/64 output ASBD and exact selected native table/entry provenance; f32 Level controls/state/text remain independent of audio precision. Stock intermediate32 Initialize precedes checked stop/deactivate/selected setup/activate/start, ready only after completion. Successful serialized offline mode changes reset voice history while retaining accepted queued timed MIDI/Level intent; failure clears readiness/pending intent and requires serialized uninitialize/initialize. Stopped32↔64 complete Level recall excludes voices/history; inherited stock Reset ignores supplied scope/element. SDK facade may normalize original ASBD size/reserved fields; no arbitrary SDK setup rollback, full wrapper fastmath/backend-fault injection, DAW/auval/device/deadline/other-platform support claim. Existing16voices,1024expanded events minus reserved state slot and1..65536prepared frames; positive opaque StartNote IDs permit1048575nonreused generations per component lifetime. No SysEx/MIDI2/pedal/pitch-bend/expression/program/editor or production distribution claim; external SDK sources remain outside RAVET and no global installation occurs.

<a id="native-gain-abi"></a>

### Native ABI for shared reference DSP

A Rust static library exposes exclusively owned gain lifecycle, prepared scratch processing and pure complete/legacy state codecs to native reference format wrappers.

**Limits:** Public gain reference only, separate 1..2 f32/f64 handles, 65,536 frames and 1,024 f32 parameter events. Shared native adapter uses at most 1 MiB f32/2 MiB f64 copied-input/output audio scratch plus events; processing panic poisons until fresh preparation. Foreign pointers/ranges and serialized ownership are caller obligations. Normal Rust callback heap behavior tested; native allocations/deadlines are outside that evidence.

<a id="gain-session-state"></a>

### Gain session save and restore

CLAP saves a complete 32-byte version-two gain/bypass record, migrates 20-byte version-one gain records, and restores both values coherently at process, flush, or reset boundaries.

**Limits:** Gain plus boolean bypass only; restore snaps smoothing, then host automation proceeds normally. Requires 64-bit atomics and fewer than 2^31 control publications across callbacks or outstanding edits. REAPER 7.82/macOS arm64 gain/bypass session recall exercised; no preset discovery or broader session compatibility claim.

<a id="editor"></a>

### Embedded editor and controls

**Limits:** Embedded Cocoa only, default 480x390 logical size, resizable through 1200x900, default optional native-editor feature. One live gain gesture at a time, bounded updates with reserved end capacity. REAPER 7.82/macOS arm64 controls/meters and FX-chain resize exercised. No plug-in-owned floating windows or general widget toolkit; floating host-wrapper corner resize unverified.

<a id="interactive-example-device-ui"></a>

### Interactive example device and MIDI ownership

Native synth/effect/MPE windows use knobs, a layered piano widget, default Audio/MIDI settings, coherent meters/voices, selected channel routing and multiple MIDI inputs; MIDI 2.0 provides an interactive codec inspector.

**Limits:** macOS live-ui feature, f32 streams with up to 64 channels and output rates 8..192 kHz; 512-frame prepared sub-blocks, 16 fixed patch commands, up to 16 MIDI inputs with 256 packets each and 64 polling attempts/block. Arrival-time MIDI/edits are block-quantized; queue loss clears voices. All four tabs uniformly scale a fixed 900x780 canvas with locked 900:780 content aspect; native viewport, component dimensions/positions and bounds checked at 720x624, 900x780, 1080x936 and constrained wide/tall requests. Explicit device selection/start; stop before changes, no automatic recovery, timestamp mapping or broad device/deadline support claim. Audio/MIDI preferences restore without automatic start; a main Start/Stop control reuses current selections.

<a id="foundry-project-management"></a>

### RAVET Foundry project creation and builds

A RAVET-native wizard and shared Rust CLI create independent offline, standalone and effect/instrument plug-in workspaces, reopen versioned TOML settings, preserve consumer source during conflict-checked regeneration and run explicit background builds/local bundles with native directory pickers.

**Limits:** Local checkout paths, offline/application/plug-in templates, immutable package/kind/processing role, bounded settings/messages/logs and one worker. Seven whitelisted directory fields, <=4096-byte paths, native modal choosers with transient sequenced selection and unchanged cancellation; macOS chooser/bridge evidence, Windows/Linux execution pending. Effect CLAP/VST3/AUv2/AUv3/AAX/LV2 and instrument CLAP/VST3/AUv2/LV2 reference adapters; external SDKs and native CMake3.25. Standalone/custom effect editor use macOS Rust window bindings. Windows x64 MSVC and Linux GTK3/WebKitGTK4.1/X11 native Foundry launchers/source-build guides supplied; target runtime validation pending. Per-file replacement, no group crash atomicity or protection against external writers; closing cancels direct child only. No MPE/component/module/platform chooser, instrument AAX/AUv3 exporters, cross/universal builds, global installation, production signing or platform/DAW/deadline claim.

<a id="reaper-validation-tools"></a>

Public ReaScript checks host discovery, parameter state, editor window creation, automation playback and saved-session recall; Python generates synthetic stereo audio and verifies actual DAW-rendered output. The native meter prototype requires a public marker and empty project before mutations.

**Limits:** Requires an empty disposable REAPER session and resource directory. Startup/evaluation/audio dialogs may need owner interaction. REAPER 7.82/macOS arm64 actual session/automation, PCM stem renders and GUI gain recording pass. Render source must be verified explicitly in the host dialog. FX-chain zoom/restore inspected; floating-wrapper corner resizing unverified. <a id="local-video-worker-frames"></a>

### Explicit bounded local-video worker frames

A separate macOS reader opens selected local video, reports first-track oriented metadata and extracts independently timestamped complete owned RGBA frames through a private AVFoundation boundary.

**Limits:** Thread-confined UI/worker API, UTF8 paths <=4096 bytes, regular files <=2 GiB, duration (0,24h], oriented dimensions 1..4096 and returned pixels <=64 MiB. Native decode allocations/I/O/time are not globally bounded. Codec/container/color conversion follow OS; requested zero timestamp tolerance may reject between-frame positions. No whole-file integrity, automatic playback/audio/AV sync/network URL/DRM/GPU view/device/other-platform/deadline claim.

<a id="metal-offscreen-rectangles"></a>

### Explicit bounded Metal offscreen rectangles

A separate macOS renderer prepares a native Metal pipeline and draws ordered portable filled rectangles with source-over blending into independent owned RGBA readback images.

**Limits:** Thread-confined UI/worker API, dimensions 1..4096, at most4096 raw rectangles, returned pixels <=64 MiB and conservative clear/covered-pixel work <=67,108,864. Coordinates clip then quantize to f32; no antialiasing or gamma/color-space transform. Native transient resources/driver work and creation/submission/wait/readback/destruction are not globally memory/time bounded. System-selected Metal GPU required, no software fallback. No window/presentation/path/text/image/rounded corners/other-platform/deadline claim.

<a id="auv2-native-control-state"></a>

### Reusable AUv2 native schema, control, text and state preflight

Apple-SDK C++17 helpers own an immutable native schema cache and isolated complete-state validator, providing full UInt32 IDs/CF metadata, canonical normalized-f32 setter preflight, complete physical text conversion and exact native-stream/AU dictionary preflight before SDK mutation; the public performance component consumes both.

**Limits:** 1..1024 global descriptors, default32 or explicit32/64 matching native companion tables; audio precision never changes normalized0..1 AU f32 controls or complete physical f32 state/text. Offsets below65536, <=128 ASCII physical parse units and native state<=8208bytes. CF metadata/text and validator lifecycle require serialized control ownership and can allocate; scalar preflight owns no SDK scheduling/notifications, rendering or host-bypass policy. Exact originating tables/library must outlive helpers. Normal framework capture Drop performs no allocation/deallocation/lock/wait or processor deactivation, including receiver early drop and asynchronous backend disposal. CPAL/OS callback closure allocation/storage/locks/destruction and panic runtime remain distinct backend/exceptional limits. Pending control poll does not wait; explicit wait joins control without deadline/cancellation. Original preparation/spawn/backend errors retain Immediate/Pending ownership, no hidden retry. Caught worker poll panic returns WorkerFault with exclusive owner after retirement; foreign deactivation panic may lose recovery and cannot manufacture success. Processing panic disables DSP permanently; recovered owner does not guarantee valid history. Option-owned consuming extraction deactivates once, requires explicit reprepare/reopen and no live mutable renderer escape. Actual converted BufferedPlaybackOutput retains unique consumer for matching stopped seeks; local silent CoreAudio20ch/96000Hz recovery/reopen plus257-frame zeroWAV44100Hz/Sinc16 retained590 drain, failed/successful seek17 and exact573 remaining drain pass. Reset pauses retaining cursor/queue; prepare does not consume/reset file. Source Failed drains prefix without EOF and original error remains on worker shutdown. Direct stopped Option-owner extraction deactivates once without read/seek/drain/join; caller-managed session hooks preserved, foreign lifecycle panics exceptional. Native clocked closure remains inaccessible, no live seek/ownership migration; recovery factory restores fresh source/DSP explicitly. <a id="integer-rate-file-playback"></a>

### Explicit integer-rate sinc scheduling for bounded-memory long file streams

Caller-selected exact integer-rate input/output scheduling extends converted read-ahead beyond the floating profile's source ceiling, with checked finite output duration, original-error ownership and stopped same-version replay.

**Limits:** No new dependency. Signal constructor accepts positive u32 rates, ratio 1/16..16 and even 16..256 taps; bounded signed relative numerator independent of duration, f64 used only for coefficient/table interpolation. Existing fixed/variable floating arithmetic and APIs remain; integer mode allows zero ppm only and reset restores exact initial phase. Equal rates still filter, fractional delay (taps-1)/2 and explicit finite padding/retained-tail policy remain, no hidden copy/trim. New mode can differ in PCM at phase boundaries; no spectral guarantee beyond scoped fixtures. Complete-file sample/clip memory limits remain. Integer read-ahead source bounds are caller usize with independent reader/container/sample caps; checked u128 retained count must fit configured u64 budget and be <=u64::MAX-65536 for largest automatic callback terminal render headroom. An oversized unused budget alone need not reject. Existing Copy/Sinc source ceiling remains 16,777,216 frames. Worker rate 1..768000/channels 1..64/batches 1..4096/arrays 32MiB and separately prepared ring limits remain. Determinable bounds reject before reader/factory I/O; committed cursor/prefix/error ownership preserved. Stopped fresh-reader replay remains O(target), bounded memory, same-version caller obligation and no cancellation/deadline; failed candidate preserves old generation/queue/phase/suffix/cursor, factory side effects not rolled back. Actual prepared output integration preserves unique consumer and explicit stopped reprepare/reopen semantics. No arbitrary-u64 terminal playback, indexed codec seek, RF64/long compressed-reader, live clock/drift, broad physical support or callback deadline claim.

An explicit known-duration integer-sinc pump rebuilds stopped WAV/AIFF output seeks from a bounded original history window, preserving old playback on candidate failure and separating source work from skipped coordinates.

Candidate validates <=taps original frames plus at most one bounded EOF probe; custom short readers use <=taps positive calls, primary full-read PCM uses ceil(window/batch). Metadata factory/backend work and latency separate. Direct failure returns original error and optional advanced candidate reader, old queue/phase/suffix/cursor/generation preserved; generic worker seek releases failed candidate on control. Rich counters separate window validation, actual cursor commits (including errors), source/padding submission after prime and absolute/per-generation output; skipped prefixes not decoded or submitted. Exact retained endpoint validates final window/EOF without priming nonexistent output; known empty supported only in new indexed pump. Temporary scratch <=66KiB plus each state's <=32MiB arrays; old/candidate coexist, reader/ring/allocator separate. Existing rate/channel/batch/container/usize and configured bounds remain, retained output <=u64::MAX-65536. Same-version content caller obligation; skipped regions not authenticated. Actual offline worker/PreparedOutput unique-consumer recovery/reprepare/pause/EOF and heap-free rendering evidence only. No compressed indexing, RF64, live callback seek/wait, clock/drift, filesystem deadline or broad physical support claim.
